metadata.title: Case Tracker: Protest and Political Violence Cases in Australia
metadata.description: Two case registers, compiled and verified separately: prosecutions and civil proceedings arising from civil protest, and proceedings concerning political violence and the state's preventive responses to it, from 2001 to 2026.
metadata.disclaimer: This tracker is a research and reference tool and does not constitute legal advice. Charges are allegations until proven; acquittals, withdrawals and appeals are recorded alongside convictions. The political violence register has no outcome or result field for a large share of its cases, because most of it concerns preventive schemes — control orders, preventative detention, post-sentence orders — that do not produce a conviction. Each record shows its sources where available and was compiled and verified on 28 August 2026.

cases.case_name: AB v Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (CTH)
cases.summary: AB, aged 17, sought bail on Commonwealth charges including doing an act in preparation for a terrorist act and using a telecommunications network to commit a serious offence. The Court found exceptional circumstances but refused bail because of an unacceptable risk of serious offending and danger to the community.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

ideology_cause: alleged mental health and suicide awareness
cases.summary: Court of Criminal Appeal appeal from refusal of bail to a 17-year-old charged over alleged Facebook threats and alleged planning/preparation for a terrorist attack in Sydney.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.
tags: alleged mental health and suicide awareness

cases.summary: The Court of Appeal considered Abbas’s appeal against sentence for conspiring with others between October and December 2016 to prepare for or plan a terrorist act in Melbourne CBD/Federation Square. The court held the sentence was not manifestly excessive and refused leave to appeal.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal against sentence refused.

cases.summary: Court of Appeal appeal against conviction and sentence for conspiracy to do acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The Court rejected challenges to the verdict and evidentiary rulings and refused leave to appeal out of time.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; leave to appeal out of time refused.

cases.summary: The Victorian Court of Appeal considered and refused Hamza Abbas’s application for leave to appeal against sentence for conspiring to do acts in preparation for or planning a terrorist act linked to the Federation Square plot.
cases.outcome: Extension of time granted; leave to appeal against sentence refused.

cases.summary: South Australian Court of Criminal Appeal appeal from a conviction for Islamic State membership. The majority held the evidence was insufficient to prove membership and set aside the conviction, entering an acquittal. Kelly J dissented and would have dismissed the appeal.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; conviction quashed; acquittal entered.

cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal allowed AH’s sentence appeal for preparation/planning of a terrorist act, found error in the original sentencing approach, and resentenced him to a shorter term.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; original sentence quashed; applicant resentenced.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal by Mohamed Al Maouie after pleading guilty to intentionally making a document connected with preparation for a terrorist act. The Court found sentencing error, re-exercised discretion, and reduced the sentence.
cases.outcome: Appeal against sentence allowed; original sentence quashed and a lower sentence imposed.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal by Omar Al-Kutobi and Mohammad Kiad from convictions for conspiring to do acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The Court upheld the appeal and resentenced both applicants.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; original sentences quashed; applicants resentenced.

cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal considered sentence appeals arising from Alameddine’s guilty pleas to possessing a revolver connected with preparation for a terrorist act and supplying that revolver to Raban Alou without authorisation. The Court allowed the appeal, set aside the original sentences, and resentenced Alameddine to 6 years for the terrorism offence and 12 years for the firearms offence.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; original sentences quashed; resentenced.

cases.case_name: Alameddine v State Parole Authority and Attorney-General of NSW
cases.summary: Judicial review of the State Parole Authority’s refusal to grant Bilal Alameddine parole on the basis that Division 3A applied to him as a terrorism-related offender.
cases.outcome: Proceedings dismissed; the parole refusal stood.

cases.case_name: Alexander v Minister for Home Affairs
cases.summary: High Court challenge to a ministerial determination under s 36B of the Australian Citizenship Act that Mr Alexander ceased to be an Australian citizen after alleged conduct involving Islamic State in Syria.
cases.outcome: Section 36B was held invalid; the plaintiff remained an Australian citizen.

ideology_cause: terrorist intimidation of Australian governments and the public
cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal allowed Almaouie’s sentence appeal in part, resentencing him for conspiracy to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act after correcting a Xiao error in discounting his plea. Firearms sentences were not disturbed.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; conspiracy sentence set aside and reduced; firearms sentences left unchanged.
tags: terrorist intimidation of Australian governments and the public

cases.summary: Sentence appeal by Raban Alou after pleading guilty to aiding and abetting Farhad Mohammad’s terrorist act, namely the shooting murder of Curtis Cheng. The Court granted leave but dismissed the appeal by majority; N Adams J dissented on manifest excess.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed by Bathurst CJ and Price J, with N Adams J dissenting only on manifest excess.

cases.case_name: Alqudsi v Commonwealth of Australia; Alqudsi v R
cases.summary: Court of Appeal challenge to the constitutional validity of s 7(1)(e) of the Crimes (Foreign Incursions and Recruitment) Act 1978 (Cth), as applied to charges that Mr Alqudsi performed services to support others entering Syria for armed hostilities.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed; declaration made that s 7(1)(e), in combination with ss 6(1)(a) and 6(3)(aa), was not invalid for exceeding the external affairs power.

cases.summary: Bail application in the Supreme Court of Victoria for a young accused charged with publishing and possessing Islamic State violent extremist material and making anti-Jewish threats by email. The Court found exceptional circumstances but refused bail because of unacceptable risk.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

cases.case_name: Application by Chief Commissioner of Victoria Police under s 21B of Part 3A of Terrorism (Community Protection) Act 2003, Re
cases.summary: Victoria Police successfully obtained Supreme Court authorisation for special powers to be exercised around the Melbourne visit of Israeli dignitaries on 12 February 2026, on the basis that the event might be targeted by a terrorist attack.
cases.outcome: Application granted; special powers authorised for the event.

cases.case_name: Application by Chief Commissioner of Victoria Police under section 21B of Part 3A of Terrorism (Community Protection) Act 2003, Re
cases.summary: Victoria Police sought and obtained Supreme Court authorisation for special powers around the 2024 Land Forces International Land Defence Exposition in Melbourne, based on reasonable grounds that the event might be the subject of a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Application granted; authorisation issued for specified special powers and time period.

cases.case_name: Application by Chief Commissioner of Victoria Police under section 21B of Part 3A of Terrorism (Community Protection) Act 2003, Re
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria authorised special police powers under s 21B of the Terrorism (Community Protection) Act 2003 (Vic) for the Pillars of Light Festival 2025 Chanukah celebration at Federation Square, Melbourne.
cases.outcome: Application granted; authorisation for special police powers made.

cases.case_name: Application By Commissioner of Australian Federal Police (No 3)
cases.summary: AFP sought forfeiture of money held in bank accounts and on travel debit cards after a restraining order had been made on suspicion the property was proceeds or an instrument of a declared-zone terrorism offence or conspiracy.
cases.outcome: Forfeiture orders were made under s 49 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (Cth).

cases.case_name: Application by Talal Alameddine pursuant to s 78 of Crimes (Appeal and Review) Act 2001 (NSW), Re
cases.summary: Talal Alameddine sought a s 78 inquiry into his sentence for intentionally possessing a revolver connected with preparation for a terrorist act and supplying that revolver to Raban Alou. The Court refused the application.
cases.outcome: Application for inquiry refused under the Crimes (Appeal and Review) Act 2001 (NSW).

cases.case_name: Application for a Preventative Detention Order in Respect of Causevic, Re
cases.summary: Victoria Police sought a Preventative Detention Order against Harun Causevic. The Supreme Court made an interim PDO, then later revoked it and ordered confidentiality/redaction arrangements for the application materials.
cases.outcome: Interim PDO made on 17 April 2015 and revoked on 21 April 2015; access to the underlying application was restricted by redaction and confidentiality orders.

cases.case_name: Application for bail by Brookman, Re
cases.summary: Brookman sought bail on charges of providing support or resources to a terrorist organisation and performing services in support of an offence under the Foreign Incursions Act. The Court found exceptional circumstances but refused bail because of unacceptable risk.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

cases.case_name: Appln for bail by Granata, Re
cases.summary: Bail application by Antonio Granata on a charge of contravening a control order. The Court granted bail subject to conditions. The judgment also summarizes Granata’s earlier guilty plea and sentence for preparatory conduct for a foreign-hostile-activities offence.
cases.outcome: Bail granted on conditions.

cases.case_name: Appln for Bail by Kocoglu, Re
cases.summary: Bail application for Isa Kocoglu, charged with providing money to support a foreign-incursion offence involving hostile activity in Syria. Bail was granted on strict conditions and a surety.
cases.outcome: Bail granted on strict conditions.

cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal granted leave to appeal but dismissed it. Atai had been sentenced for aiding a terrorist act (the murder of Curtis Cheng), making funds available to Islamic State on two occasions, and an ISIS membership offence taken into account on sentence.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; sentence upheld.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Commonwealth Attorney-General sought urgent interlocutory orders to abridge service and list an application for an interim supervision order (and potentially later an extended supervision order) against Amin, who had earlier pleaded guilty to terrorism-preparation and export offences. The Court granted short service and listed the ISO application for hearing.
cases.outcome: Application for abridgment of time granted; ISO application listed for hearing.

cases.case_name: Attorney General of Commonwealth of Australia v Pender (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made a 3-year extended supervision order against Blake Nicholas Pender after finding he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence.
cases.outcome: ESO granted.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Commonwealth Attorney-General sought a further extended supervision order against Nacer Benbrika. Elliott J found Benbrika posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence and made a 7 month 18 day extended supervision order with therapeutic conditions only.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order made.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made an interim supervision order by consent for Nowroz Amin pending determination of the Commonwealth Attorney-General’s application for an extended supervision order. The application was based on Amin’s earlier terrorism-preparation offending and assessed risk of future serious Part 5.3 offending.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made by consent for 28 days; matter stood over for further hearing; court appointed an expert and required an affidavit explaining delay.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Attorney-General sought an extended supervision order and an interim supervision order for Nacer Benbrika, including additional restrictions (the Further Conditions). The Court granted leave to amend the applications but refused to include the Further Conditions in the interim order. The Director-General’s public interest immunity objection to disclosure of sensitive security information was upheld.
cases.outcome: Leave to amend the originating motion and summons was granted; the further conditions were not imposed in the third interim supervision order; the Director-General’s objection to disclosure of secret information was upheld.

cases.summary: Preliminary hearing on the Commonwealth’s application for an extended supervision order and interim supervision order in respect of Blake Nicholas Pender, a convicted terrorist offender. The Court ordered an interim supervision order for 28 days and appointed two experts to assess risk.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order granted; experts appointed; protective orders over confidential material had already been made.

cases.summary: The Court dismissed a jurisdictional objection and made an interim supervision order against Khaled Temssah, a terrorist offender who had pleaded guilty in 2021 to preparing to travel to Kashmir for hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Jurisdictional objection dismissed; interim supervision order made and imposed for 28 days.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria considered the Commonwealth Attorney-General’s application for an extended supervision order against Khaled Temssah after he completed a terrorism sentence. The Court found he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence and ordered an 18-month ESO.
cases.outcome: ESO granted; interim supervision orders had previously been made.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of South Australia granted the Attorney-General’s application for a 12-month extended supervision order against Mr Cromb, a terror suspect serving a sentence for possessing terrorist-material documents.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order granted for 12 months.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of South Australia considered, and declined to make, an interim supervision order against Anthony Paul Dobson. The Court accepted he was a high-risk offender but found the material did not establish an appreciable risk justifying an extended supervision order on the then-available evidence.
cases.outcome: Application for an interim supervision order refused; medical examination/report order made.

cases.case_name: Attorney-General of Commonwealth of Australia v Amin (Final)
cases.summary: The Attorney-General sought an extended supervision order against Nowroz Amin after his release from custody following terrorism-related convictions. The Court considered whether he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence and dismissed the application.
cases.outcome: Application for an extended supervision order dismissed; interim supervision order expired on delivery of judgment; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.case_name: Attorney-General of Commonwealth of Australia v Ghazzawy
cases.summary: Commonwealth application for an interim supervision order under s 105A.9A of the Criminal Code after Ghazzawy served a sentence for making a document connected with preparation of a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made for 28 days.

cases.case_name: Attorney-General of Commonwealth of Australia v Ghazzawy (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW considered and dismissed the Attorney-General’s application for a 12-month extended supervision order against Ibrahim Ghazzawy. The Court held the statutory risk test was not met, quashed the interim supervision order extension, and ordered costs against the Commonwealth.
cases.outcome: Application for an extended supervision order dismissed; interim supervision order extension quashed; costs awarded to the defendant.

cases.case_name: Attorney-General of Commonwealth of Australia v Pender
acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court reviewed the extended supervision order imposed on Blake Pender, considered whether the scheduling conditions were reasonably necessary and appropriate, and varied the order while otherwise affirming it.
cases.outcome: ESO varied to adopt Annexure A conditions; order otherwise affirmed; recommendation made that Community Corrections provide ongoing psychologist support for at least 6 months.

cases.summary: The Commonwealth Attorney-General sought an extended supervision order and interim supervision order for Hadashah Sa’Adat Khan after her sentence for providing support to a terrorist organisation. The Court made an interim supervision order pending determination of the extended supervision order application.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made on 25 August 2022; ESO application to proceed to later trial.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria made an extended supervision order for Hadashah Sa'adat Khan for 18 months after finding she posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence similar to her prior support offence.
cases.outcome: ESO granted.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court corrected published reasons to redact identifying details of a man involved in the defendant’s earlier terrorism-support offence.
cases.outcome: Order made for redaction of the man’s name and two related identifying names from the reasons for judgment.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria made and then refined suppression/confidentiality orders in proceedings concerning the variation and affirmation of an extended supervision order for Ms Sa’adat Khan.
cases.outcome: The Court made orders varying and otherwise affirming the extended supervision order, and later made confidentiality orders governing filing, access and redaction of materials.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Attorney-General sought and obtained a suppression order preventing publication of the defendant’s case manager’s name, because disclosure could endanger safety, undermine the effectiveness of terrorism supervision orders, and prejudice national security.
cases.outcome: Suppression order granted.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: Periodic review of Ms Sa’adat Khan’s extended supervision order. The Court varied several conditions and otherwise affirmed the order after finding she remained an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence. The underlying terrorist offending involved providing support to Islamic State by helping facilitate Paul Jensen’s travel to Syria to join the organisation.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order affirmed with variations.

cases.summary: Review of a bail/extradition order in relation to a charge of attempting to provide support or resources to a terrorist organisation.
cases.outcome: Application for review dismissed.

cases.case_name: Azari v R; Al-talebi v R
cases.summary: Sentence appeals by Omarjan Azari and Ali Al-Talebi arising from convictions for Islamic State funding/support offences and, for Azari, a terrorist-act planning offence.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal against sentence granted, but both appeals dismissed.

acts_engaged: Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act 1987 (Cth)
cases.summary: BA sought a certificate under the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act so the Attorney-General could request FBI-held documents for use in a committal concerning two federal terrorism-related charges, including providing support to Islamic State.
cases.outcome: Certificate granted; the court held it was in the interests of justice for the Attorney-General to request the documents from the USA.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal concerning Mr Baladjam’s 2008 guilty pleas to four Commonwealth terrorism-preparation and extremist-material possession offences arising from conduct in Sydney in 2005.
cases.outcome: Extension of time granted; leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed; sentence left undisturbed.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria replaced Benbrika’s continuing detention order with an extended supervision order, imposed conditions, and ordered it to run for one year. The Court also found the AFP Minister’s non-disclosure of exculpatory material to be a serious interference with the administration of justice.
cases.outcome: ESO granted; CDO replaced; one-year duration; conditions imposed; non-disclosure referred to the INSLM.

cases.case_name: Benbrika v Minister for Home Affairs
cases.summary: The Victorian Court of Appeal dismissed Abdul Nacer Benbrika’s appeal against a continuing detention order. The Court held he remained an unacceptable risk of committing serious Part 5.3 offences if released, and that no less restrictive measure would be effective.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; continuing detention order confirmed.

cases.case_name: Benbrika v Minister for Home Affairs
acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: Appeal proceedings and interlocutory application concerning a continuing detention order made against Abdul Nacer Benbrika under the Criminal Code.
cases.outcome: The Court dealt with the appellant’s application for funding/costs orders pending appeal and indicated an interim costs order would be made if Commonwealth funding was not available.

cases.case_name: Benbrika v Minister for Home Affairs
cases.summary: High Court held s 36D of the Australian Citizenship Act invalid insofar as it empowered the Minister to revoke Benbrika’s citizenship after his terrorism convictions, because it conferred an exclusively judicial punitive function on the Executive.
cases.outcome: s 36D invalid; declaration that Benbrika remains an Australian citizen; costs against respondents.

cases.summary: Court of Appeal appeal from convictions and sentence for a Melbourne-based terrorist organisation matter involving membership, direction, resources, funds, and possession connected with preparation for a terrorist act. Convictions were partly allowed (notably Benbrika count 12 and Joud counts 7-8), and sentences were resentenced.
cases.outcome: Appeal of first and second accused allowed in part; retrial ordered for Benbrika count 12; Joud counts 7 and 8 set aside with acquittals; appeals against conviction otherwise dismissed; accused resentenced.

cases.case_name: Betka v R; Ghazaoui v R; Hawchar v R (No 3)
cases.summary: The Court corrected resentencing orders for Bilal Betka. The underlying qualifying matter was his terrorism conviction and sentence for engaging in hostile activity in a foreign country.
cases.outcome: Orders were varied to correct the commencement date and to impose a single non-parole period taking account of the earlier federal sentence.

cases.summary: Federal Court confirmed, without variation, an interim control order imposed on Zainab Abdirahman-Khalif to protect the public from terrorism-related risk and prevent support or facilitation of terrorist acts.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation and continued in force until 4 May 2022.

cases.summary: The Federal Court made an interim control order against Mehmet Biber after finding on the balance of probabilities that he had provided support for or otherwise facilitated hostile activity in Syria. The reasons relied on his Syria travel and assistance to others, later communications and online material, and his associations after return to Australia.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made; confirmation hearing listed.

cases.summary: The Federal Court granted an interim control order against Adam Brookman. The order was made because he had been convicted of a terrorism-related offence involving support services for foreign fighters in Syria and was assessed as posing ongoing risks of terrorism- and hostile-activity-related conduct.
cases.outcome: Application for interim control order granted.

cases.summary: The Federal Court varied an interim control order so that its controls would not apply while the respondent remained in custody, and made ancillary confidentiality orders.
cases.outcome: Application granted; interim control order varied and confidentiality orders made.

ideology_cause: hostile activity in a foreign country
cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed an interim control order imposed on Adam Mathew Brookman after being satisfied he had been convicted of a terrorism-related offence and/or had provided support for or facilitated hostile activity in a foreign country.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation.
tags: hostile activity in a foreign country

ideology_cause: violent overthrow of the Southern Philippines government
cases.summary: The Federal Court granted an interim control order against Paul Dacre under s 104.4 of the Criminal Code, relying on his prior Victorian conviction for preparing for incursions into a foreign country for hostile activities.
cases.outcome: Application for an interim control order granted.
tags: violent overthrow of the Southern Philippines government

ideology_cause: hostile activity in a foreign country
cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed an interim control order made against the respondent on 12 May 2021. The court was satisfied the respondent had been convicted of a terrorism offence and had provided support for or otherwise facilitated hostile activity in a foreign country.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed with variations; in force until 11 May 2022.
tags: hostile activity in a foreign country

cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed, with some variations, an interim control order imposed on Paul James Dacre under the Criminal Code. The order was based on his terrorism-related conviction for preparing for an incursion into a foreign country for hostile activities.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed subject to variations.

cases.summary: The Federal Court made an interim control order against Radwan Dakkak under s 104.4 of the Criminal Code after his convictions for associating with Islamic State-linked persons and organisations. The Court modified several proposed controls and ordered the matter listed for confirmation.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made, with amendments to some controls; matter listed for confirmation hearing.

cases.summary: Federal Court application for and grant of an interim control order against Antonino Granata, relying on his terrorism/hostile-activity conviction arising from a Philippines incursion plot.
cases.outcome: Application for interim control order granted in part; some proposed controls were refused or left for further evidence/submissions, and the matter was adjourned for a confirmation hearing.

cases.summary: Federal Court confirmation of an interim control order against Antonino Alfio Granata after his conviction for preparing incursions into the Philippines for hostile activities.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed with minor variations and extended until 2 June 2021.

cases.summary: Federal Court interim control order made against Kadir Kaya after his conviction for preparing for incursions into the Philippines for hostile activities. The Court accepted he had engaged in conduct connected with a foreign-hostile-activity plot and imposed extensive restrictions to reduce future risk.
cases.outcome: Interim Control Order granted; matter adjourned for case management and possible confirmation hearing.

ideology_cause: hostile activity in a foreign country
cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed an interim control order made against Kadir Kaya, with some variations, after accepting he had been convicted of a terrorism-related offence and that the order’s conditions were reasonably necessary and adapted to protective purposes.
cases.outcome: Control order confirmed subject to variation.
tags: hostile activity in a foreign country

cases.summary: The Federal Court granted an interim control order against Murat Kaya, after finding his 2019 conviction for preparation for incursion into the Southern Philippines for hostile activities was an offence relating to terrorism and that he had provided support for hostile activity in a foreign country.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made; curfew adjusted from 10 pm–6 am to 12 am–6 am.

cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed an interim control order made against Murat Kaya under s 104.4 of the Criminal Code, with agreed terms and a one-year duration.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed with variations.

ideology_cause: hostile activity in a foreign country
cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed, without variation, an interim control order made against Belal Saadallah Khazaal on 26 August 2020.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation.
tags: hostile activity in a foreign country

cases.summary: The Federal Court granted an interim control order against Ahmad Saiyer Naizmand. The order was sought by the AFP after his release from custody, relying on his prior terrorism-related convictions and the need to protect the public and prevent support for terrorism.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made substantially in the terms proposed, with one objection resolved in the respondent’s favour.

ideology_cause: hostile activity in a foreign country
cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed, with variations, an interim control order made against Ahmad Saiyer Naizmand. The respondent did not contest confirmation. The order was imposed on the basis of a prior terrorism-related conviction and to protect the public from terrorist activity and related support/facilitation.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed and varied by consent; suppression/non-publication orders made.
tags: hostile activity in a foreign country

cases.summary: Federal Court application by the AFP for an interim control order against Alo-Bridget Namoa after her conviction for conspiring to do acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The Court found the control order conditions satisfied and made the order.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made.

cases.summary: Federal Court confirmation, without variation, of an interim control order made against Alo-Bridget Namoa. The order was confirmed on the basis that she had been convicted of a terrorism-related conspiracy.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation to remain in force until 18 December 2020.

ideology_cause: hostile activity in a foreign country
cases.summary: The Federal Court granted the AFP’s application for an interim control order against Shayden Jamil Thorne, finding the statutory preconditions satisfied and that the controls were reasonably necessary and appropriate to protect the public and prevent support for terrorist or hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Application granted; interim control order made; confirmation hearing listed.
tags: hostile activity in a foreign country

cases.summary: Federal Court confirmation of an interim control order against Shayden Jamil Thorne, with agreed terms and further variations. The Court was satisfied the statutory requirements were met and confirmed the order until 5 March 2021.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed with further variations.

cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed an interim control order made against Shayden Jamil Thorne, continuing restrictions for 12 months to protect the public from terrorist activity and related support or facilitation.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed for the maximum period of 12 months.

cases.case_name: BP v State of New South Wales
cases.summary: Appeal from orders appointing experts and imposing an interim supervision order on BP under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court ultimately revoked leave to appeal out of time and dismissed the proceedings after the supervision order was revoked and the underlying matter discontinued.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal out of time revoked; proceedings dismissed. Costs left for later determination, with no order as to costs indicated tentatively.

cases.case_name: Browne v Assistant Commissioner of Police, North West Metro Region
cases.summary: Federal Court judicial review of a Melbourne CBD designated-area declaration under the Control of Weapons Act, including Charter and implied-freedom challenges. The Court held the declaration invalid and unlawful, but upheld s 10KA(1).
cases.outcome: Declaration invalid and unlawful; Charter breach found; implied-freedom challenge rejected.

cases.summary: Phillip Galea was sentenced after being found guilty of planning attacks on left-wing targets and attempting to make the 'Patriot’s Cookbook', a document intended to facilitate violent acts.
cases.outcome: Sentenced to a total effective term of 12 years’ imprisonment with a non-parole period of 9 years.

cases.case_name: Chaarani v Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth)
cases.summary: The Court of Appeal refused leave to appeal from the trial judge’s refusal to suppress publication of guilty verdicts in a terrorism-conspiracy trial, where the applicants also faced further terrorism charges in a second trial.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal refused; no suppression order made.

cases.summary: The Court of Appeal considered whether arson and attempted arson were available alternative verdicts to Commonwealth terrorist-act charges arising from two mosque burnings at the Imam Ali Islamic Centre, Fawkner.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal was granted, but the convictions were upheld and the appeals dismissed.

cases.summary: The Court of Appeal considered leave to appeal and resentencing for Abdullah Chaarani’s federal terrorism sentences. It modified the sentence for the Federation Square conspiracy by reducing cumulation, but refused leave to appeal the mosque offending sentence.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed in part; Beale sentence modified; leave to appeal the Tinney sentence refused.

cases.summary: Appeal from interlocutory orders in proceedings for an extended supervision order under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), where the State relied on a Facebook post linked to Islamic State to classify the appellant as a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; the Court upheld the preliminary orders for psychiatric and psychological examinations and an interim supervision order.

cases.case_name: CMHV and Director-General of Security and Minister for Foreign Affairs, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The AAT reviewed and affirmed ASIO’s adverse security assessment and the Minister for Foreign Affairs’ decisions to cancel CMHV’s Australian passport and require surrender of his Turkish travel documents. ASIO and the Minister acted on suspicions that CMHV might travel to Turkey and then Syria to engage in politically motivated violence or support it.
cases.outcome: Decisions affirmed.

cases.case_name: Commissioner of Australian Federal Police v Khazaal
cases.summary: The Federal Court varied Mr Belal Khazaal’s confirmed control order so that its obligations, restrictions and prohibitions would not apply while he remained in custody.
cases.outcome: Application granted; control order varied.

cases.case_name: Commissioner of Police, NSW v Taleb (No 2)
cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on subpoenas and public interest immunity in Moudasser Taleb’s criminal case concerning alleged preparatory conduct toward entering Syria for hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Commissioner’s claim for public interest immunity upheld; redacted disclosure held to satisfy prior production orders.

cases.case_name: Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions v Galea (Ruling No 1)
cases.summary: Pre-trial subpoena ruling in Phillip Galea’s prosecution for two terrorist offences. The court set aside most defence subpoenas for lacking a legitimate forensic purpose.
cases.outcome: Most June 2019 defence subpoenas were set aside.

cases.case_name: Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions v Saadieh
cases.summary: The Court of Criminal Appeal refused the Commonwealth DPP’s detention application and confirmed Joseph Saadieh’s conditional bail on a charge of being a member of Islamic State from 12 June 2018 to 18 June 2021.
cases.outcome: Detention application refused; bail confirmed.

cases.case_name: Cromb v R; Pay v R
cases.summary: The Court of Appeal dismissed sentence appeals by Cromb and Pay, who had each pleaded guilty to possessing extremist documents likely to assist a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Permission to appeal granted, but both sentence appeals dismissed.

cases.summary: Civil claim for damages arising from the 18 April 2015 Operation Rising raid on the Cruse family home, during which police unlawfully arrested and used force against Eathan Cruse in a counter-terrorism operation. The Court held the arrest unlawful, found batteries and an assault by words, and awarded damages.
cases.outcome: Judgment for the plaintiff. The Court held the arrest unlawful and the force unnecessary and unreasonable; police committed batteries and an assault. Damages awarded.

cases.summary: Appeal against severity of sentence for five offences arising from a single intoxicated episode in which the applicant threatened and assaulted victims, resisted police, and stabbed a police dog while avoiding apprehension.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal allowed; original sentences quashed; applicant re-sentenced to a lower overall term.

cases.case_name: CXQY and Director-General of Security, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The AAT reviewed and affirmed ASIO’s adverse security assessment against CXQY in connection with his Australian citizenship application, finding he was at least likely to engage in politically motivated violence and upholding the resulting prohibition on approval of citizenship.
cases.outcome: Adverse security assessment affirmed.

cases.case_name: D v Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth)
cases.summary: Full Court appeal from refusal to make suppression orders in a terrorism-advocacy prosecution. The Court held the videos and identifying material should be suppressed until further order, subject to a limited exception for pixelated imagery.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; suppression orders made.

cases.summary: Court of Appeal considered whether particulars of a joint charge under s 119.4(1) of the Criminal Code were adequate. Majority refused leave to appeal; Priest JA would have allowed it.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal refused by majority (Maxwell ACJ and Kyrou JA); Priest JA dissented.

cases.summary: Court of Appeal judgment on an appeal against conviction and sentence for five arsons at a police station, churches, a bakery and a childcare centre in January-February 2011. The convictions were largely upheld; sentence was varied on re-sentencing.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal against conviction was refused except on one evidentiary ground, but the appeal was dismissed; the appellant was re-sentenced.

cases.summary: Mustafa Dirani appealed his conviction and sentence for conspiracy to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act. The Court of Criminal Appeal allowed the appeal on an evidentiary ground, quashed the conviction, and ordered a new trial.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; conviction quashed; new trial ordered. Sentence appeal not considered.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth) (DPP) v Ali
cases.summary: Appeal by the DPP against sentence for one count of doing an act in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The Court held the original sentence was manifestly inadequate and resentenced the respondent.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; respondent resentenced.

cases.case_name: DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC PROSECUTIONS (CTH) v ARAN SHERANI (RULING NO 1)                                                                                                                                                                                     BC202318603
cases.summary: Ruling on a s 138 application to exclude evidence said to be obtained through Aran Sherani’s allegedly unlawful arrest and ensuing searches in a terrorism prosecution.
cases.outcome: Application to exclude evidence refused.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth) v Besim
cases.summary: Crown appeal against sentence for Sevdet Besim’s guilty plea to preparing or planning a terrorist act. The Court found the original sentence manifestly inadequate and increased it to 14 years with a 10 year 6 month non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; sentence set aside and respondent resentenced.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth) v El Sabsabi
ideology_cause: support for anti-Assad / anti-Syrian-government hostile activities
cases.summary: Crown appeal against sentence imposed for two charges of performing acts preparatory to the commission of a foreign incursion offence. The Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal and upheld a 44-day custodial term on one charge and a two-year community correction order on the other.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; sentences upheld.
tags: support for anti-Assad / anti-Syrian-government hostile activities

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth) v Thomas
cases.summary: Commonwealth DPP appealed a Chief Magistrate’s grant of bail to Joseph Thomas on charges including receiving funds from and providing support or resources to Al Qa’ida. Teague J dismissed the appeal and upheld bail.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; bail order stood.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth) v Thomas
cases.summary: Joseph Terrence Thomas was sentenced after a jury found him guilty of intentionally receiving funds from a terrorist organisation and possessing a falsified passport. The court described his earlier travel to Pakistan/Afghanistan, Al Qa’ida training, and later dealings with Al Qa’ida operatives as the background to the offending.
cases.outcome: Convicted on count 1 (receiving funds from a terrorist organisation) and count 4 (falsified passport); acquitted on counts 2 and 3. Sentenced to five years’ imprisonment total, with a two-year non-parole period.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth) v Thomas (Ruling No 5)
cases.summary: The Court considered and refused the Commonwealth's application to revoke Joseph Thomas's bail pending trial on terrorism and passport charges.
cases.outcome: Application to revoke bail refused; bail continued on the same terms.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth) v Thomas (Ruling No 7)
acts_engaged: National Security Information (Criminal and Civil Proceedings) Act 2004 (Cth)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria considered whether National Security Information Act closure and non-publication orders should continue into the jury trial in Thomas’s terrorism prosecution. Cummins J declined to extend the 29 September 2005 orders beyond empanelment.
cases.outcome: Application to continue the national-security closure/non-publication orders was refused.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Besim (No 3); Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v MHK (a Pseudonym) (No 3)
cases.summary: Court of Appeal re-sentencing in two terrorism-preparation convictions; the Court held div 105A continuing detention provisions did not alter the appropriate sentences.
cases.outcome: Crown appeals against sentence were allowed earlier; on this further hearing the Court held the new continuing detention regime did not justify changing the re-sentences.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Brookman (Ruling No 1)
cases.summary: The court ruled on duplicity, particulars and between-dates charging for two terrorism-related counts: one alleging support or resources to Islamic State in Syria, and one alleging services to a Chechen foreign-fighter group to support hostile activity in Syria.
cases.outcome: Charges held not bad for duplicity; further particulars refused; Crown required to prove persistent conduct sufficient for each continuing enterprise charge.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Brookman (Ruling No 3 - AGD PII)
cases.summary: Public interest immunity ruling in a terrorism-related prosecution of Adam Mathew Brookman concerning subpoenaed mutual-assistance and disclosure materials.
cases.outcome: The Court upheld the Attorney-General’s Department public interest immunity claims over the disputed documents.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Dirani
cases.summary: The Court revoked Mustafa Dirani’s bail and refused bail on the Commonwealth’s detention application, finding an unacceptable risk he would commit serious offences if released. The underlying matter was an alleged conspiracy to prepare for the Curtis Cheng shooting.
cases.outcome: Bail revoked and refused; suppression/non-publication order made.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Fattal
cases.summary: Court of Appeal dismissed convictions and sentence appeals arising from a conspiracy to prepare for and plan an armed terrorist attack on Holsworthy Barracks.
cases.outcome: All conviction and sentence appeals were dismissed; the DPP’s sentence inadequacy appeal was also dismissed.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Karabegovic
cases.summary: Interlocutory Crown appeal about the construction of s 101.4 of the Criminal Code in six counts alleging possession of 'Inspire' magazines connected with assistance in a terrorist act. Leave to appeal was granted but the appeal dismissed.
cases.outcome: Court held Benbrika remained applicable; the appeal on the construction of s 101.4 was dismissed.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v MD
cases.summary: Commonwealth DPP appeal against bail granted to an 18-year-old charged with collecting a document likely to facilitate terrorist acts and importing an ISIS flag. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal and upheld bail with strict conditions.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; bail upheld.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v MHK (A Pseudonym) (No 1)
cases.summary: Crown appeal against a 7-year sentence for a 17-year-old who pleaded guilty to planning and preparing to build and detonate bombs in a populated area to further Islamic State’s cause. The Court allowed the appeal and resentenced him to 11 years with an 8-year-3-month non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; sentence increased on resentencing.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Saadieh
cases.summary: The Supreme Court considered a bail application for Joseph Saadieh, who was charged with intentionally being a member of ISIS/ISIL between 12 June 2018 and 18 June 2021. The Court found exceptional circumstances and granted conditional bail, later stayed.
cases.outcome: Conditional bail granted; stay ordered for 7 days.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth) v Sherani
cases.summary: The offender pleaded guilty to being a member of Islamic State and was convicted of doing acts in preparation for a terrorist act. The Court sentenced him to four years for membership and seven years for the preparation offence, with a total effective sentence of eight years and a six-year non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced on Charge One and Charge Four.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (NSW) v GX
cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal granted the Director’s detention application and refused the respondent bail pending sentence on multiple assault and assaulting-law-officer charges, relying partly on evidence of extremist associations and threats.
cases.outcome: Detention application granted; conditional bail refused.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) v Sewell
cases.summary: The Victorian Court of Appeal heard the Director’s appeals against the sentences imposed on Thomas Sewell and Jacob Hersant for violent disorder. The Court dismissed Sewell’s appeal, found Hersant’s sentence manifestly inadequate but exercised its residual discretion not to interfere, and dismissed the appeal overall.
cases.outcome: Appeals dismissed; Sewell’s sentence left undisturbed, and Hersant’s sentence not interfered with despite error being found.

cases.case_name: Director of Public Prosecutions v Thomas (Ruling No 3)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria ruled admissible an AFP interview of Joseph Terrence Thomas conducted in Pakistan on 8 March 2003 for his terrorism trial.
cases.outcome: Interview admitted in evidence at jury trial.

cases.case_name: DPFX and Director-General of Security, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The Tribunal reviewed and affirmed ASIO’s adverse security assessment against the applicant, finding reasonable grounds based on his associations with SWAN and his misleading/disclosed information in security interviews.
cases.outcome: ASA affirmed.

cases.summary: Commonwealth DPP appeal against bail granted to a 14-year-old respondent charged with alleged terrorist organisation membership and advocating terrorism. The Court dismissed the appeal and upheld bail subject to strict conditions.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; bail grant stood.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court allowed the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions’ appeal, set aside the magistrate’s grant of bail, and refused bail on a fresh hearing.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; bail revoked; fresh bail application refused.

cases.summary: Sentencing for a deliberate vehicle-ramming attack in the Melbourne CBD that killed one pedestrian and injured many others.
cases.outcome: Offender sentenced to life imprisonment for murder, with concurrent sentences for the remaining offences and a 30-year non-parole period.

cases.summary: Appeal against sentence for engaging in conduct preparatory to a foreign incursion offence. The applicant travelled to Turkey intending to cross into Syria to join and fight for Islamic State, was detained by Turkish police, and pleaded guilty to s 119.4(1). The Court granted leave but dismissed the appeal.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed. Sentence left unchanged.

cases.case_name: Elomar v R; Hasan v R; Cheikho v R; Cheikho v R; Jamal v R
cases.summary: Five appellants appealed convictions for conspiring to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act or acts in Sydney between July 2004 and November 2005. The Court of Criminal Appeal dismissed all conviction appeals and all sentence appeals.
cases.outcome: Appeals against conviction dismissed; leave to appeal against sentence granted but each sentence appeal dismissed.

cases.case_name: FLSZ and Director-General of Security, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The AAT reviewed ASIO’s adverse security assessment concerning FLSZ and affirmed it. ASIO assessed FLSZ as directly or indirectly a risk to security, relying on material including Facebook posts, associations with persons of concern, and doubts about travel-related conduct.
cases.outcome: Decision affirmed; adverse security assessment upheld.

cases.summary: The Federal Court granted an interim control order against Tyler Slavko Jakovac after his conviction for intentionally advocating the doing of a terrorist act or terrorism offence. The Court held the statutory preconditions were met and imposed extensive preventive controls to reduce risk of support for or facilitation of terrorism.
cases.outcome: Application granted; interim control order made.

cases.summary: The Federal Court considered whether to confirm an interim control order made against Tyler Jakovac. After hearing evidence of his changed circumstances, the Court revoked the order rather than confirm it.
cases.outcome: Interim control order revoked; confirmation refused.

cases.summary: The Federal Court considered an application for an interim control order against Mr Homewood on his release from custody. The Court accepted the need for the order, including conditions limiting internet use and electronic monitoring, to manage risks of terrorist activity and ammunition acquisition.
cases.outcome: Interim control order to be made in principle; applicant to file short minutes including the statement of grounds before final chambers orders.

cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed, without variation, an interim control order made against Wade John Homewood. The Court was satisfied he had been convicted of a terrorism-related offence and that the control order conditions remained reasonably necessary and adapted to protect the public from a terrorist act or prevent support for or facilitation of such an act.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation; confirmed control order to operate until 19 March 2025.

cases.summary: The Federal Circuit Court considered and refused an oral application to transfer an interim control order confirmation hearing to the Federal Court. It held the issuing court must determine the confirmation hearing and adjourned the matter.
cases.outcome: Transfer application refused; proceeding adjourned for later hearing; costs reserved.

cases.summary: The Court confirmed, with variation, an interim control order against Harun Causevic under Division 104 of the Criminal Code, finding it would substantially assist in preventing a terrorist act. The order was based on alleged involvement in an Anzac Day 2015 terrorist plot in Melbourne.
cases.outcome: Interim Control Order confirmed and varied; some controls removed.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal by Ibrahim Ghazzawy for making a document connected with preparation for a terrorist act. The Court found error in the original sentence, allowed the appeal, and resentenced him.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; original sentence quashed; applicant resentenced to 8 years' imprisonment with a 6-year non-parole period.

cases.case_name: Haddara v Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth)
cases.summary: Bail application by Amer Haddara, charged with intentionally being a member of a terrorist organisation. The Court found exceptional circumstances were not shown and dismissed bail.
cases.outcome: Bail refused; application dismissed.

cases.case_name: Hammoud v Director of Public Prosecutions (Vic)
cases.summary: Bail application by Shoue Hammoud pending trial on terrorism charges was refused under the statutory presumption against bail.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

cases.case_name: Hamzy v Commissioner of Corrective Services NSW
cases.summary: Court of Appeal appeal about the legality of prison restrictions on an EHRR inmate’s visits to his chosen lawyer and the monitoring of lawyer telephone calls, and a separate challenge to English-language requirements in visits, correspondence and calls.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed in part. Clauses 94(3) and the drop-in policy were held not to apply to lawyer communications as challenged; the RDA-based challenge was dismissed.

cases.summary: An AAT freedom-of-information review about AFP and CDPP documents relating to Dr Mohamed Haneef’s 2007 terrorism investigation, arrest, charging, detention, visa cancellation, and the later discontinuance of proceedings.
cases.outcome: The Tribunal affirmed, varied, or set aside various FOI exemption claims over documents connected with the Haneef investigation.

cases.case_name: Hardy v State of New South Wales
acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Court of Appeal dismissed Hardy’s appeal against a further extended supervision order. The court upheld findings that he was an eligible offender who had advocated support for violent extremism and posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; extended supervision order upheld.

cases.summary: The Court of Criminal Appeal considered whether the applicant’s sentence for engaging in hostile activity in Syria was manifestly excessive, and whether the operation of s 19ALB (parole restriction for terrorism-related matters) warranted reduction of the head sentence.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal allowed; sentence reduced while the non-parole period remained unchanged.

cases.summary: Simon Hickey sought a Supreme Court direction under s 176 of the Crimes (Administration of Sentences) Act 1999 that the State Parole Authority had revoked his statutory parole order on false, misleading or irrelevant information. The Court dismissed the application.
cases.outcome: Application for direction dismissed; no costs order.

cases.summary: Interlocutory appeal by the accused against a ruling admitting evidence in a prosecution for possessing Inspire magazine Issue 9 in connection with assistance in a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Application for leave to appeal refused; the trial judge’s evidentiary ruling stood.

cases.summary: Appeal against sentence for advocating terrorism and a related ammunition storage offence. The Court held the original sentences were affected by error, allowed the appeal, quashed the District Court sentences, and resentenced the applicant to 2 years 4 months with a 1 year 9 month non-parole period for the terrorism offence, and 5 months concurrent imprisonment for the ammunition offence.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; original sentences quashed; resentenced.

cases.summary: Court of Appeal decision on sentence appeal. The appellant pleaded guilty to using a carriage service offensively and transmitting violent extremist material on Telegram and Instagram over 4–12 June 2024. The appeal challenged the 2 year 6 month sentence for the violent extremist material count.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal concerning four offences sentenced by Johnson J and two offences sentenced by Culver DCJ. The Court upheld some grounds, resentenced the applicant on the prisoner assault and Bayda offences, and varied commencement dates.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted in both matters; appeals allowed in part; some sentences set aside and replaced; threat-to-kill and terrorism-preparation sentences otherwise left standing.

cases.case_name: Hussain v Minister for Foreign Affairs
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: Federal Court appeal from AAT review of a passport cancellation and ASIO adverse security assessment. The assessment said the applicant might, if he travelled overseas, participate in or support others involved in politically motivated violence.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed. No order as to costs.

cases.case_name: HUTCHINSON v ROADS AND TRAFFIC AUTHORITY, NSW BC200655054
cases.summary: FOI review concerning 53 photographs of the Sydney Harbour Bridge withheld by the Roads and Traffic Authority as restricted documents affecting counter-terrorism measures.
cases.outcome: The Tribunal affirmed the Roads and Traffic Authority’s refusal of access.

cases.summary: Appeal against sentence for a juvenile offender who pleaded guilty to conspiring to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act in Sydney in November-December 2014. The Court allowed the appeal after holding the sentencing judge erred in failing to account for the utilitarian value of the guilty plea, and resentenced the offender.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal allowed; sentence re-exercised and reduced.

cases.case_name: INQUEST INTO THE DEATH OF TYLER JORDAN CASSIDY BC201113048
cases.summary: Coronial inquest into the death of Tyler Jordan Cassidy, who was shot by police at All Nations Park, Northcote on 11 December 2008 after arming himself with knives, making threats, and confronting officers.
cases.outcome: The coroner found Tyler died from a gunshot wound to the chest and could not determine which officer fired the fatal bullet. The inquest also made findings about the shooting and police response.

acts_engaged: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth) Division 102 — proscription regime
cases.summary: The Federal Magistrates Court made an interim control order against David Matthew Hicks under Division 104 of the Criminal Code. The order was based on findings that he had trained with Lashkar-e-Tayyiba and al-Qa’ida and that restrictions were reasonably necessary to protect the public from a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made.

acts_engaged: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth) Division 102 — proscription regime
cases.summary: Federal Magistrates Court confirmation of an interim control order made against David Matthew Hicks. The Court found the order would substantially assist in preventing a terrorist act and that Hicks had received training from listed terrorist organisations.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed and varied.

acts_engaged: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth) Division 102 — proscription regime
cases.summary: The Federal Magistrates Court made an interim control order against Joseph Terrence Thomas after finding he had received training from Al Qa’ida and that the order would substantially assist in preventing a terrorist act. Some proposed restrictions were refused or left for further modification.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made; proposed obligations 9(a), 9(b) and the unmodified form of 6(a) were not accepted.

cases.summary: The court decided whether the confirmation hearing for an interim control order made on 27 August 2006 should be transferred to the Federal Court. It held the matter should remain in the Federal Magistrates Court and dismissed the transfer application.
cases.outcome: Application to transfer the proceeding to the Federal Court dismissed.

cases.case_name: Jarrett v State of New South Wales
cases.summary: The Court of Appeal held invalid NSW provisions creating public assembly restriction declarations (PARDs) and associated effects on public assemblies, finding they impermissibly burdened the implied freedom of political communication.
cases.outcome: Declarations of invalidity made; costs ordered for plaintiffs.

cases.case_name: Joud v R; Benbrika v R; Raad v R; Sayadi v R
cases.summary: Interlocutory appeal against refusal of a permanent stay of a terrorism-conspiracy trial. The Court held the autrefois convict plea failed, rejected the double-jeopardy argument standing alone, but found the judge had erred by treating the accused collectively on oppression and remitted the stay application.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; stay application remitted to the trial judge for reconsideration.

cases.case_name: K v Children's Court of Victoria
cases.summary: Judicial review of a Children’s Court decision that exceptional circumstances justified hearing a minor’s terrorism-related charges by committal rather than summarily. The Supreme Court dismissed the application and upheld the uplift order.
cases.outcome: Application for judicial review refused; Children’s Court uplift order upheld.

cases.case_name: Kaya v Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions
cases.summary: Bail applications by Murat Kaya and Antonino Alfio Granata on a joint Commonwealth charge alleging preparatory conduct for foreign travel to the Philippines to engage in hostile activity. The Court found exceptional circumstances but refused bail because of unacceptable risk.
cases.outcome: Bail refused for both applicants.

cases.summary: Bail application by Murat Kaya on a Commonwealth terrorism charge alleging preparatory acts to facilitate travel for hostile activity in Syria, northern Iraq, or as later framed, the Philippines. Bail was refused.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

cases.summary: Shane Kent applied for bail while awaiting retrial on terrorism charges, including intentionally being a member of a terrorist organisation, providing resources to that organisation, and making a document connected with preparation for a terrorist act. Bail was granted on the basis of exceptional delay, and the court found no unacceptable risk shown.
cases.outcome: Bail granted.

cases.case_name: KFDJ and Director General of Security, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The Tribunal reviewed ASIO’s adverse security assessment and associated passport-cancellation request concerning KFDJ. It upheld the assessment, with minor textual variations, finding the information and recommendations justified on security grounds.
cases.outcome: Assessment and grounds upheld subject to deletion of the words 'or a foreign country' in specified clauses; passport-cancellation review left for later hearing.

cases.case_name: KFDJ and Minister for Foreign Affairs, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The Tribunal affirmed the Minister for Foreign Affairs’ decision to cancel KFDJ’s passport after accepting ASIO’s adverse security assessment and finding that his past violent extremist conduct and intended travel to Ukraine raised security concerns.
cases.outcome: Decision affirmed; passport cancellation upheld.

cases.case_name: Khalid v Legal Aid Commission of NSW
cases.summary: Judicial review of Legal Aid NSW’s decision to assign legal aid in a terrorism-conspiracy prosecution to a Serious Criminal Law Panel solicitor rather than the plaintiff’s long-time solicitor.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.summary: The Court of Criminal Appeal allowed the applicant’s sentence appeal because the sentencing judge failed to account for the utilitarian value of the guilty plea. The sentence was reduced from 22 years 6 months with a 16-year 9-month non-parole period to 20 years with a 15-year non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal allowed; sentence set aside and re-sentenced.

cases.summary: Appeal against sentence for engaging in a terrorist act by stabbing Wayne Greenhalgh multiple times in Sydney on 10 September 2016. The Court held the sentence was not manifestly excessive and dismissed the appeal.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed.

cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal considered Mahmoud Khayat’s appeal against conviction for conspiracy to do acts in preparation for, or planning, terrorist acts. The appeal challenged unanimity directions and the use of alleged lies as consciousness of guilt. The Court granted leave out of time on ground 1, refused leave on ground 2, and dismissed the appeal.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed. Leave granted out of time and to appeal on ground 1; leave refused on ground 2.

cases.summary: Federal Court judicial review of the Attorney-General’s refusal to make a parole order for Belal Saadallah Khazaal, following a terrorism-related conviction. The Court held procedural fairness was afforded and dismissed the application.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; no denial of procedural fairness established.

cases.summary: Appeal in a terrorism-document case involving Belal Khazaal’s compilation and publication of an e-book said to assist a terrorist act. The Court of Criminal Appeal allowed the appeal on a jury-direction issue and ordered a new trial on the conviction count.
cases.outcome: By majority, the conviction was quashed and a new trial ordered. Leave to appeal against sentence was granted but the sentence appeal was not ultimately the operative order.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal in Belal Saadallah Khazaal’s terrorism matter. The Court of Criminal Appeal granted leave to appeal but dismissed the appeal, leaving intact the 12-year sentence with a 9-year non-parole period for making a document connected with assistance in a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal against sentence dismissed.

cases.case_name: LAWRENCE v NEW SOUTH WALES                                                                                                                         BC202019519
cases.summary: The NSW Court of Appeal dismissed Mr Lawrence’s appeal against an interim detention order under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW) and rejected his constitutional challenge to the Act.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; Act held constitutionally valid.

ideology_cause: extremist Islamic ideology supportive of religiously motivated violence
cases.summary: The Federal Court granted an interim control order against Abdul Nacer Benbrika, finding his prior Australian terrorism convictions satisfied the statutory threshold and that the proposed controls were reasonably necessary and adapted for public protection and preventing support for terrorism or hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Interim control order granted; suppression order made.
tags: extremist Islamic ideology supportive of religiously motivated violence

cases.case_name: Lelikan v Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) (Cth)
acts_engaged: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth) Division 102 — proscription regime
cases.summary: Bail release application for Renas Lelikan, charged with being a member of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) between 17 December 2005 and 23 October 2015. The court found exceptional circumstances and granted bail subject to strict conditions.
cases.outcome: Release application granted; bail allowed subject to conditions.

cases.summary: Federal Court judicial review of the Attorney-General’s 2020 refusal to grant parole to Faheem Lodhi, a terrorism-offence offender. The Court upheld the decision and dismissed the application.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; parole refusal upheld.

cases.summary: Appeal by Faheem Khalid Lodhi against refusal to quash a terrorism indictment. The Court held the retrospective amendments did not apply to his already-commenced criminal proceedings and that the indictment failed to plead essential elements, so the indictment was quashed and the matter remitted.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; indictment quashed; matter remitted to Whealy J.

cases.summary: Faheem Khalid Lodhi appealed convictions for collecting documents, doing an act, and possessing a thing connected with preparation for a terrorist act, and appealed sentence. The Court dismissed the conviction appeal and granted but dismissed leave to appeal against sentence.
cases.outcome: Appeal against conviction dismissed; leave to appeal against sentence granted and sentence appeal dismissed.

cases.summary: Civil negligence proceeding alleging Victoria Police breached duties in monitoring and managing the terrorism risk posed by Hassan Khalif Shire Ali before the Bourke Street attack. The Court struck out the pleadings but granted leave to replead.
cases.outcome: ACSC struck out; plaintiffs granted leave to replead.

cases.summary: The Federal Court made an interim control order against Abdirahman-Khalif under s 104 of the Criminal Code after finding it would substantially assist in preventing a terrorist act or support for it. The order was made on the basis of her attempted travel to Turkey/Syria to support IS, her possession and access to IS propaganda, communications with IS supporters, and related conduct.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made; proposed Control 9 was not imposed.

cases.summary: The Federal Court varied and confirmed an interim control order against Zainab Abdirahman-Khalif after finding that confirmation would substantially assist in preventing a terrorist act or support/facilitation of one.
cases.outcome: Interim control order varied and confirmed; Control 2 removed and curfew varied to midnight–6am.

cases.summary: Federal Court granted an interim control order against EB after finding he had been convicted in Australia of an offence relating to terrorism and had provided support for or otherwise facilitated hostile activity in a foreign country.
cases.outcome: Application granted; interim control order made, with confirmation hearing listed.

cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed, without variation, an interim control order made against EB. The Court was satisfied EB had been convicted of an offence relating to terrorism and had provided support for or facilitated hostile activity in a foreign country, and that the order’s restrictions were reasonably necessary and adapted to prevent support for terrorism or hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation.

cases.summary: The Federal Court considered and made a new interim control order against Radwan Dakkak under s 104.4 of the Criminal Code, relying on his prior convictions for associating with terrorist organisations and a later contravention of the first interim control order.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made, subject to stated qualifications.

cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed an interim control order against Radwan Dakkak, with a minor variation, after finding he had been convicted in Australia of terrorism-related offences and that the controls were reasonably necessary to protect the public from a terrorist act and prevent support for or facilitation of a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed and varied.

cases.case_name: Messenger v Commonwealth of Australia (Represented by Dept of Finance)
cases.summary: Federal Court employment case involving adverse action, underpayment, and coercion claims. One factual strand concerned a death threat to the senator’s Burnie office and ensuing security concerns.
cases.outcome: All applications dismissed; no adverse action, underpayment, or coercion contraventions established.

cases.case_name: Minister for Corrections NSW v Elomar (No 2)
cases.summary: Judicial review of the State Parole Authority’s decision to grant Ahmad Elomar parole. The Court rejected the Minister’s challenge, finding no jurisdictional error and dismissing the summons.
cases.outcome: Stay vacated; summons dismissed; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.case_name: Minister for Home Affairs v Benbrika
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria made a continuing detention order detaining Abdul Nacer Benbrika for three years after finding he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence if released and that no less restrictive measure would be effective.
cases.outcome: Continuing detention order granted.

cases.case_name: Minister for Home Affairs v Benbrika
cases.summary: The High Court considered whether Div 105A of the Criminal Code, allowing continuing detention orders for terrorist offenders, was constitutionally valid. A majority held it was valid and answered the reserved question 'No'.
cases.outcome: Reserved constitutional question answered 'No'; Div 105A upheld. Respondent to pay applicant’s costs.

cases.case_name: Minister for Home Affairs v Benbrika (First review)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria reviewed Mr Benbrika’s continuing detention order under Division 105A of the Criminal Code. The Court affirmed the order for a further period, finding he still posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence and that no less restrictive measure was effective.
cases.outcome: CDO affirmed on review.

cases.case_name: Minister for Home Affairs v Benbrika (No 2)
acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: Review of a continuing detention order made against Abdul Nacer Benbrika under the Criminal Code. The judge declined to sit on the review, making no definitive recusal ruling but deciding it was prudent not to hear the matter.
cases.outcome: Judge decided not to sit in the CDO review; another judge was to be allocated.

cases.case_name: Minister for Home Affairs v Benbrika (Ruling No 1)
acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria decided evidentiary admissibility issues in a Commonwealth continuing detention order application against Abdul Nacer Benbrika. The Court held the challenged evidence admissible and not subject to exclusion or limitation.
cases.outcome: All challenged evidence admitted; no exclusion under s 135 and no limitation under s 136.

cases.case_name: Minister for Home Affairs v Pender
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW ordered that Blake Nicholas Pender be subject to a continuing detention order for one year from 13 September 2021, finding he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 offence if released.
cases.outcome: Continuing detention order made.

cases.case_name: Minister for Home Affairs v Pender (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW considered the Minister for Home Affairs’ preliminary application for a continuing detention order against Blake Nicholas Pender, and ordered psychiatric/psychological experts to assess him for the CDO proceeding. The Court also made protective non-publication orders over sensitive documents.
cases.outcome: Application for appointment of experts granted; protective orders made; proceedings adjourned.
