cases.summary: The Court of Appeal allowed an appeal against cumulation, finding the total effective sentence of 38 years infringed totality. It resentenced the applicant to a total effective sentence of 32 years with a non-parole period of 24 years.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; cumulation reduced; resentenced.

cases.case_name: Moutia Elzahed v Commonwealth and NSW
cases.summary: Four plaintiffs sued the Commonwealth and NSW over the manner of executing a search warrant at their home on 18 September 2014. The court found the force used by AFP and NSW Police was reasonable and entered verdicts for both defendants.
cases.outcome: All claims failed; verdicts entered for the defendants.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal by Ahmad Naizmand after guilty pleas to five counts of contravening a control order. The Court found error in the original discount approach, re-sentenced, and dismissed the appeal.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed; original sentence left in place after re-sentencing exercise.

cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal dismissed Alo-Bridget Namoa’s appeal against conviction for conspiring with Sameh Bayda to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act. The appeal challenged fresh evidence and a spousal-immunity argument.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted on ground 1; appeal dismissed.

cases.summary: High Court appeal about whether spouses can be guilty of conspiracy under s 11.5 of the Criminal Code (Cth) for conspiring to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act. The appeal was dismissed and the conviction stood.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; the High Court held spouses can be guilty of conspiracy under s 11.5.

cases.summary: The State of New South Wales sought a preliminary order and ultimately an extended supervision order against Alam as a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender. Wilson J held the statutory preconditions were not established to the required degree of probability and dismissed the summons.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; no supervision order made.

cases.case_name: NEW SOUTH WALES v BAREZ                                                                                                                         BC201910163
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales granted an interim supervision order for Edris Barez for 28 days pending final hearing, and ordered compliance with supervision conditions plus psychiatric and psychological examinations.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order granted under the THRO Act.

cases.summary: Costs decision in NSW proceedings brought by the State against Cody Nigel William Church under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW) seeking an interim supervision order and an extended supervision order. The Court ordered the State to pay the defendant’s costs, including the preliminary hearing.
cases.outcome: Plaintiff ordered to pay defendant's costs of the proceedings, including the preliminary hearing, as agreed or assessed.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court considered whether George Dickson should be made subject to an extended supervision order. The Court found his prior threatening material and statements advocated support for terrorist acts, but was not satisfied to a high degree of probability that he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence, so the summons was dismissed and the interim supervision order discharged.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed; interim supervision order discharged; file access restricted.

cases.summary: NSW sought an extended supervision order against Amin Elmir after his conviction for preparing to enter Syria to engage in hostile activity. The Court found he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence and made an extended supervision order, but for 12 months rather than 3 years.
cases.outcome: Application granted in part. Extended supervision order made for 12 months with conditions in Schedule A.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted an Interim Supervision Order against Ahmed Elomar under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017, after finding the alleged matters capable of supporting an extended supervision order.
cases.outcome: Interim Supervision Order granted and conditions imposed.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made an interim supervision order against Ahmed Elomar under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017, and appointed a psychiatrist and psychologist for examinations in support of an extended supervision order application.
cases.outcome: ISO granted; expert examinations ordered; access to file restricted; conditions imposed.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales made an interim supervision order against Mr Elzamtur under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), on a provisional basis pending final determination.
cases.outcome: Interim Supervision Order made; expert report orders also made.

cases.summary: New South Wales sought a third extended supervision order and, pending determination, an interim supervision order against Christopher Hardy. The Court found the statutory preconditions satisfied and made the interim order with conditions, including expert examinations and supervision requirements.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order granted; experts appointed; conditions imposed and amended as to the movement-schedule condition.

cases.summary: Preliminary hearing on the State’s application for an interim detention order or interim supervision order against Simon Hickey under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court found the supporting material would not, if proved, justify the orders and dismissed the summons.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.case_name: NEW SOUTH WALES v HOLT (NO 7)                                                                                                                                                                                     BC202319754
cases.summary: Interlocutory evidentiary ruling in ongoing proceedings under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), admitting the Corner Report into evidence.
cases.outcome: Objection to the Corner Report was overruled and the report was admitted into evidence without limitation.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted an interim supervision order and appointed two experts to assess Monzor Ibrahim under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW).
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made for 28 days; qualified psychiatrist and registered psychologist appointed to examine the defendant.

cases.case_name: NEW SOUTH WALES v LAWRENCE                                                                                                                         BC201918381
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales granted the Attorney General’s terrorism intelligence application concerning seven documents about Tukiterangi Lawrence under the THRO Act, and made confidentiality orders for the substantive proceedings.
cases.outcome: Application allowed; confidentiality orders made under s 59C.

cases.case_name: NEW SOUTH WALES v LAWRENCE                                                                                                                         BC201918383
cases.summary: The Supreme Court considered the State’s application for interim detention or supervision orders under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW) against Tukiterangi Lawrence, found the supporting material sufficient, and made an interim detention order subject to stay pending a constitutional issue.
cases.outcome: Interim detention order granted (stayed pending constitutional issue).

cases.case_name: NEW SOUTH WALES v LAWRENCE (NO 2)                                                                                                                         BC201918380
cases.summary: The Supreme Court determined a costs application arising from an Attorney General’s terrorism intelligence application under s 59A of the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The Court ordered the Attorney General to pay the defendant’s costs thrown away caused by the adjournment, including half of preparatory costs and all costs of the hearing day.
cases.outcome: Costs ordered in favour of the defendant.

cases.summary: Preliminary hearing on admissibility of police intelligence for an interim supervision order application against the defendant under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court admitted the material for the preliminary stage.
cases.outcome: Annexure A to the affidavit of Jamie McLaughlin was admitted into evidence at the preliminary hearing.

cases.summary: The State appealed from the refusal to make an extended supervision order against Mohamed Naaman. The Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal, holding the State had not established an unacceptable risk of him committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; interim supervision order set aside; costs ordered against the State.

cases.case_name: NEW SOUTH WALES v OSMAN                                                                                                                                                                                     BC202019526
cases.summary: The State sought an extended supervision order and interim supervision order against Maywand Osman. The Court held the preliminary threshold was met and made orders appointing experts and imposing an interim supervision order.
cases.outcome: Application for preliminary THRO Act orders granted.

cases.summary: The State of New South Wales sought an extended supervision order against RC. Garling J held the State had not proved to a high degree of probability that RC posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence, so the application was dismissed.
cases.outcome: Application for an extended supervision order refused and dismissed.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales conducted a preliminary hearing under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2007 (NSW) concerning Mr Richardson. The Court held that a clinical psychologist’s report assessing his risk of violent extremism/terrorism was admissible for the preliminary hearing and admitted it into evidence.
cases.outcome: Risk assessment report admitted into evidence for the preliminary hearing.

cases.summary: The State sought a two-year extended supervision order against Richardson under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The Court held he was not a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender and was not shown to pose an unacceptable terrorism-offending risk, so the summons was dismissed and the interim order discharged.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; interim supervision order discharged; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted an interim supervision order and related examination orders under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act against Mr Richardson, based on alleged plans to kill Aboriginal men and other racially motivated violent statements made in custody.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made; expert examinations ordered.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made a two-year extended supervision order against Ricky White under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The Court found he was a convicted NSW underlying terrorism offender and terrorism activity offender because of a 2016 church arson and 2014 anti-Semitic threats, and that he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order granted for two years with extensive conditions.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made an interim supervision order against Ricky White, appointed a psychiatrist and psychologist to examine him, and imposed extensive supervision conditions pending final determination. The order was based on his prior terrorism-context arson, threatening calls to the Sydney Jewish Museum, and related extremist affiliations.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made; experts appointed; access to file restricted.

cases.case_name: NEW SOUTH WALES v XX                                                                                                                         BC202221214
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made a 28-day Interim Supervision Order and related examination orders against XX under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), finding the supporting material would justify an ESO if proved.
cases.outcome: ISO and examination orders granted; conditions imposed.

cases.summary: The Federal Court granted an interim control order against Ahmad Saiyer Naizmand, imposing extensive restrictions to protect the public from terrorism and prevent support for or facilitation of terrorist acts or hostile activity overseas.
cases.outcome: Interim control order granted; one proposed counselling control rejected; confirmation hearing listed.

cases.case_name: Nicolson v Naizmand (duration of non-publication order)
cases.summary: Federal Court interlocutory judgment determining that a non-publication order in an interim control order proceeding could not run 'until further order' and instead should be limited to 10 years.
cases.outcome: Final non-publication order made for a fixed 10-year period ending 15 May 2036; court held it had no power to make an indefinite final NPO.

cases.summary: Sentence appeal concerning Saeed Noori’s deliberate driving of a vehicle into pedestrians at a Melbourne CBD intersection, killing one person and injuring many others. The Court refused leave to appeal and upheld life imprisonment with a 30-year non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal refused; sentence upheld.

cases.case_name: NSW Council for Civil Liberties Inc v Classification Review Board (No 2)
cases.summary: Judicial review of Classification Review Board decisions refusing classification to two publications, Join the Caravan and Defence of the Muslim Lands, because they were found to promote or incite crime, violence and terrorist acts.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; refusal classifications upheld.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made a two-year extended supervision order against Mr Ahsan Kamal Cheema under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), finding he was a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender and posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order granted.

cases.summary: The State sought an extended supervision order against XX. Fagan J held the statutory eligibility requirements were met, but was not comfortably satisfied that XX posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence. The summons was dismissed and the interim supervision order discharged.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed; interim supervision order discharged; costs ordered against the State.

cases.case_name: Osman v State Parole Authority & Attorney General of New South Wales
cases.summary: Judicial review of the State Parole Authority’s 10 July 2020 refusal to grant parole to Maywand Osman, a terrorism-related offender. The Court held the Authority did not err and dismissed the summons.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed; costs ordered against the plaintiff, subject to further costs submissions.

cases.case_name: Plaintiff S111A/2018 v Minister for Home Affairs (No 4)
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: Federal Court judicial review of ASIO’s 2018 and 2020 adverse security assessments against the plaintiff, both connected to alleged EIJ/al-Qaeda activity and risk to security. The Court upheld major procedural fairness and legal unreasonableness challenges.
cases.outcome: Judicial review allowed in part; the Court indicated the 2018 and 2020 ASAs were invalid and should be set aside, with further orders to be made.

cases.summary: Nine accused sought injunctions, suppression orders and a temporary stay in response to media reporting connected with a terrorism conspiracy trial. The Court refused the applications.
cases.outcome: Summons and stay application dismissed; limited suppression of the decision and application details ordered for the time being.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court held that the fitness-to-plead issue in the terrorism conspiracy prosecution could be determined by a judge alone under s 11 of the Mental Health (Criminal Procedure) Act 1990 (NSW), and that this did not infringe s 80 of the Commonwealth Constitution.
cases.outcome: Constitutional challenge rejected; judge-alone determination of fitness to plead permitted.

cases.summary: Pre-trial constitutional challenge by Khaled Cheikho in a nine-accused terrorism conspiracy prosecution, seeking to exclude telecommunications interception evidence and invalidate s 18(2) of the Telecommunications (Interception) Act 1979 (Cth).
cases.outcome: The court held that s 18(2) was constitutionally valid and dismissed the motion.

cases.summary: Ruling on admissibility of the ‘Melbourne evidence’ in a Sydney terrorism conspiracy trial involving alleged preparation for terrorist acts, extremist instruction, and related associative conduct.
cases.outcome: The Court declined to exclude the Melbourne evidence.

cases.summary: Bail application by Mohamed Ali Elomar in ongoing Commonwealth terrorism proceedings. The court refused bail, finding no exceptional circumstances.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales refused a stay application brought by one accused in a terrorism prosecution. The issue was whether ASIO officers could lawfully give surveillance evidence with the Director-General's approval under the ASIO Act.
cases.outcome: Application for stay of proceedings dismissed/refused.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW determined public interest immunity claims over surveillance, listening-device, and search-warrant material sought by an accused in a terrorism conspiracy prosecution, ultimately excusing the Crime Commission from production.
cases.outcome: Public interest immunity upheld; production refused.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW refused an application to change venue in a nine-person terrorism conspiracy trial, finding Parramatta suitable despite defence and Crown concerns about distance, security and courtroom facilities.
cases.outcome: Change-of-venue application refused.

cases.summary: Pretrial ruling on admissibility of conversations and other evidence in a nine-accused conspiracy prosecution alleging preparation for terrorist acts.
cases.outcome: Held the challenged evidence was admissible as circumstantial evidence of the existence and scope of the conspiracy, and in some instances potentially as acts in furtherance.

cases.summary: Nine accused were charged with conspiracy to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act or acts. The court rejected applications to dismiss the charge, quash the indictment for duplicity, and strike it as an offence unknown to law.
cases.outcome: Applications refused; indictment challenge dismissed.

cases.summary: Pretrial application in a terrorism conspiracy prosecution seeking removal of a fixed glass dock screen to avoid prejudice and secure a fair trial.
cases.outcome: Application granted; the fixed dock screen was ordered removed for the purposes of the trial.

cases.summary: Pretrial voir dire ruling on Khaled Cheikho’s application to exclude statements and seized material in the Sydney terrorism conspiracy case. The court held the statement and seized material were admissible and dismissed the motion.
cases.outcome: Notice of motion dismissed; challenged statement and seized material admitted.

cases.summary: Application to disqualify the trial judge for apprehended bias in a Commonwealth terrorism-conspiracy trial; the application was refused.
cases.outcome: Disqualification application refused.

cases.summary: The court considered whether evidence of Moustafa Cheikho’s alleged Lashkar-e-Taiba training in Pakistan and related identification evidence could be admitted in the trial of nine men charged with conspiring to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Evidence of LeT training and identification evidence admitted against Moustafa Cheikho; not admitted at that stage against the other accused.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on whether the accused Khaled Sharrouf’s fitness hearing should be before judge alone or judge and jury in a prosecution for conspiracy to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Held that the amended Mental Health (Criminal Procedure) Act applied, so fitness was to be determined by judge alone.

cases.summary: Five offenders were sentenced after a jury found them guilty of participating in a conspiracy to prepare for a terrorist act or acts in Australia, involving ammunition, chemicals, laboratory equipment, extremist material and concealment steps.
cases.outcome: Sentences of imprisonment were imposed on all five offenders with substantial non-parole periods.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling in the Operation Pendennis terrorism case on whether a compact disc seized from Aimen’s premises and later imaged/retained by police should be excluded under s 138 Evidence Act.
cases.outcome: Evidence not excluded; admissible at trial.

cases.summary: Application to discharge the jury was brought in a Sydney terrorism conspiracy trial after publicity from the Melbourne Benbrika sentencing. The court refused the application, finding no real risk of unfair trial from the publicity.
cases.outcome: Application to discharge the jury refused.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court found Khaled Sharrouf unfit for trial, but also found a prima facie case on a single-count indictment alleging conspiracy with others to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Accused found unfit to be tried; prima facie case established; detained in MRRC Screening Unit until fit for trial.

cases.summary: The court ruled on subpoenas served on the AFP and NSW Police in Hamdi Alqudsi’s terrorism prosecution, largely allowing production subject to limits and later public-interest-immunity questions.
cases.outcome: Subpoena not set aside; several paragraphs limited or rejected, with public interest immunity reserved.

ideology_cause: support for anti-Syrian Government armed conflict
cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling in proceedings against Hamdi Alqudsi for allegedly directing the activities of a terrorist organisation (the Shura) in relation to domestic terrorism targets. The Court rejected a stay for autrefois convict/double jeopardy/oppression and granted public interest immunity over sensitive police material.
cases.outcome: Proceedings were not dismissed or stayed; public interest immunity was granted.
tags: support for anti-Syrian Government armed conflict

cases.summary: Pretrial ruling on admissibility and stay application in a terrorism prosecution alleging that the accused directed a terrorist organisation and was affiliated with Islamic State/Shura.
cases.outcome: Permanent stay refused; record of interview to be amended as specified.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: Hamdi Alqudsi was sentenced after trial for intentionally directing the activities of the Shura, a terrorist organisation operating in Sydney. The conduct included meetings, target discussions, and planning for possible terrorist attacks.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Bail variation and detention application concerning a juvenile charged with conspiracy to prepare or plan a terrorist act. The Court deleted a private electronic monitoring condition, granted bail on amended conditions, and dismissed the Commonwealth’s detention application.
cases.outcome: Variation to delete private electronic monitoring granted; bail granted on the terrorism charges with amended conditions; detention application dismissed.

cases.summary: Tyler Jakovac was sentenced in the District Court of NSW after pleading guilty to intentionally advocating terrorist acts or terrorism offences online over about 11 months through Telegram channels and chat groups, with extremist, racist and jihadist-violent content.
cases.outcome: Convicted on a guilty plea and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Bail application by a 16-year-old charged with conspiring to engage in an act in preparation for or planning a terrorist act. The Court found exceptional circumstances and no unacceptable risk, and granted bail subject to conditions.
cases.outcome: Bail granted subject to conditions.

cases.summary: Radwan Dakkak was sentenced for contravening an interim control order by accessing prohibited electronic media. The court also recounted his earlier convictions for associating with Islamic State members in support of that terrorist organisation.
cases.outcome: Convicted on the ICO breach count and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Sentencing for a guilty plea to conspiracy to do acts in preparation for or planning a terrorist act. The conspiracy involved Abbas, his brother, cousin and a friend preparing a Melbourne CBD terrorist attack using explosives, bladed weapons and possibly firearms.
cases.outcome: Convicted on plea of guilty and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Pre-trial rulings on extensive prosecution evidence in a conspiracy to do acts in preparation for or planning a terrorist act allegedly involving an attack in Melbourne CBD/Federation Square area.
cases.outcome: The judge ruled on admissibility of videos, images, messages, travel evidence and other material; the accused were later tried and convicted, but this judgment itself is a rulings judgment.

cases.case_name: R v Abbas, Chaarani and Mohamed
cases.summary: Three offenders were convicted of conspiring with Ibrahim Abbas to prepare or plan a terrorist act in Melbourne in late 2016. The Court found the contemplated attack involved mass slaughter in Melbourne CBD around Christmas 2016, with IEDs, bladed weapons, firearms and reconnaissance. The judgment also references earlier convictions of Chaarani and Mohamed for burning the Imam Ali Islamic Centre.
cases.outcome: Convictions for the conspiracy were followed by substantial prison sentences; the Court also noted existing terrorism sentences for Chaarani and Mohamed.

cases.summary: High Court appeal from a conviction for intentionally being a member of Islamic State. The Court held the jury could infer the respondent intentionally took steps to become a member, and allowed the Crown’s appeal.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; Full Court orders set aside; conviction appeal dismissed.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The offender pleaded guilty to doing an act in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The court sentenced him to 12 years' imprisonment with a 9-year non-parole period, backdated to 24 April 2016, and ordered juvenile detention until age 21.
cases.outcome: Convicted on plea and sentenced for the terrorism preparation/planning offence.

cases.case_name: R v Al-Kutobi; R v Kiad
cases.summary: The offenders pleaded guilty to conspiring between about 1 January and 10 February 2015 to prepare for or plan a terrorist act. Garling J found the conspiracy was ongoing at arrest and included plans to damage a building with an IED and to use a bladed weapon to kill or seriously harm an unidentified person.
cases.outcome: Each offender sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment with a 15-year non-parole period.

cases.summary: Ali Khalif Shire Ali pleaded guilty to intentionally doing an act in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The court sentenced him for planning a New Year’s Eve mass-casualty attack in Melbourne, involving firearm acquisition enquiries, reconnaissance, and other preparatory conduct.
cases.outcome: Convicted on a plea of guilty and sentenced for a terrorist act preparation/planning offence.

cases.summary: Raban Alou was sentenced for aiding and abetting Farhad Mohammad’s terrorist act in Parramatta on 2 October 2015. The court found Alou helped obtain a firearm, sought an Islamic State flag, and supplied the loaded revolver to Mohammad, who then killed Curtis Cheng outside NSW Police Headquarters.
cases.outcome: Convicted on guilty plea; sentenced to 44 years’ imprisonment with a 33-year non-parole period.

ideology_cause: Sunni Islamist militant conflict in Syria
cases.summary: Hamdi Alqudsi was sentenced after a jury convicted him of seven counts of performing services for persons with the intention that they enter Syria to engage in armed hostilities. The court found he coordinated travel, communications, and contact with Syria-based handlers for multiple men over several months.
cases.outcome: Convicted on seven counts and sentenced to imprisonment with a total effective sentence and non-parole period.
tags: Sunni Islamist militant conflict in Syria

ideology_cause: support for armed hostilities in Syria
cases.summary: Pretrial ruling admitting search-warrant evidence in a seven-count prosecution alleging that Hamdi Alqudsi provided services to assist named men to travel from Australia to Syria to engage in armed hostilities.
cases.outcome: Search evidence admitted under s 138 of the Evidence Act 1995 (NSW).
tags: support for armed hostilities in Syria

cases.case_name: R v Alqudsi; Alqudsi v Commonwealth of Australia
ideology_cause: support for armed hostilities in Syria
cases.summary: A constitutional challenge to s 7(1)(e) of the Crimes (Foreign Incursions and Recruitment) Act 1978 (Cth), brought in proceedings linked to an indictment alleging Hamdi Alqudsi provided assistance to seven men travelling from Australia to Syria to engage in armed hostilities.
cases.outcome: The Court held s 7(1)(e) valid and dismissed the accused’s motion and the declaratory summons.
tags: support for armed hostilities in Syria

cases.summary: The offender was sentenced after pleading guilty to doing acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act, and attempting to export prohibited Tier 1 goods advocating a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Aggregate sentence imposed for both offences.

cases.summary: The offender pleaded guilty to committing acts in preparation for incursions into Syria for hostile activities. The Court found he had taken serious preparatory steps, was significantly radicalised, and sentenced him to 5 years 5 months with a 4 years 1 month non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Convicted on guilty plea and sentenced for the s 119.4(1) foreign-incursion preparation offence.

cases.summary: Izzydeen Atik was sentenced after pleading guilty to intentionally being a member of a terrorist organisation and providing resources to it by arranging air travel. The court imposed partially concurrent prison terms and a non-parole period, taking account of guilty plea, assistance, mental illness and intellectual disability.
cases.outcome: Sentence imposed on both terrorism counts; partial concurrency; discount for assistance and undertaking to cooperate.

cases.summary: Pre-trial stay application in a prosecution arising from a 15 September 2014 telephone conversation alleged to be preparation for a terrorist act and a conspiracy to murder.
cases.outcome: Application granted; indictment stayed until the Commonwealth DPP elects which count to proceed with.

cases.summary: The court refused an application to discharge the jury in Omarjan Azari’s terrorism trial. The issue was whether evidence about Azari’s alleged involvement in a prior Queensland attack plan was admissible to prove his intent in a 15 September 2014 telephone call alleged to be an act in preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Application to discharge jury refused.

acts_engaged: Court Suppression and Non-publication Orders Act 2010 (NSW)
cases.summary: Suppression-order ruling in Omarjan Azari’s terrorism trial, where he had pleaded not guilty to one count of doing an act in preparation or planning for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Suppression orders were granted; the Phelan affidavit was to be returned to the Commissioner and replaced with a redacted version.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court ruled on admissibility of evidence in Omarjan Azari’s terrorism trial. The charge concerned an alleged telephone conversation in which Azari participated in planning a terrorist act in Australia, said to involve killing random members of the public.
cases.outcome: Evidence describing items found at Agim Kruezi’s home was admitted; photographs in VD8 were excluded.

acts_engaged: Court Suppression and Non-publication Orders Act 2010 (NSW)
cases.summary: Supreme Court ruling granting suppression and pseudonym orders in Omarjan Azari’s pending terrorism-preparation/planning prosecution.
cases.outcome: Application for suppression and non-publication orders granted; the witness was anonymised as 'Max Marid' and related material was restricted.

cases.summary: Evidentiary ruling on whether intercepted telephone calls were admissible in Azari’s trial for doing an act in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: The Court ruled that calls 5, 15, 39 and 201 were inadmissible, and permitted only limited facts about call 201.

cases.summary: Suppression, pseudonym and closed-court orders were made in Omarjan Azari’s terrorism trial to protect a witness and national security interests.
cases.outcome: Application granted; the Court made pseudonym, closed-court and suppression orders.

cases.summary: Pretrial ruling on whether the jury should be discharged after a witness identified a juror in a terrorism-preparation trial against Omarjan Azari.
cases.outcome: Application to discharge the jury was dismissed; the trial was ordered to continue with 11 jurors.

cases.case_name: R v B; sub nom B v R (FLR)
cases.summary: Court of Criminal Appeal refused leave to appeal against interlocutory rulings refusing to quash an indictment charging conspiracy to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act or acts.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal refused on duplicity, consent, and offence-unknown-to-law grounds.

cases.case_name: R v Bayda; R v Namoa (No 3)
cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on whether a conspiracy charge for preparing or planning a terrorist act could stand against two accused who claimed to be spouses.
cases.outcome: Application for a permanent stay of the conspiracy proceedings was dismissed.

cases.case_name: R v Bayda; R v Namoa (No 8)
acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: Bayda and Namoa were convicted by jury of conspiring to do acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act between 8 December 2015 and 25 January 2016 in Sydney and elsewhere. The court sentenced both to imprisonment.
cases.outcome: Guilty verdicts followed by sentence for conspiracy to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria sentenced Abdul Nacer Benbrika and six co-offenders after jury convictions for membership of a terrorist organisation and related terrorism offences. The court treated the matter as an embryonic violent-jihad organisation that fostered and prepared a future terrorist act, though no target had been selected.
cases.outcome: Convictions entered and sentences imposed for terrorism offences; Benbrika received the highest aggregate sentence.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria considered whether a new conspiracy trial against Benbrika and others was barred or should be stayed because of earlier terrorism convictions. The Court held the elements were not identical, but stayed the proceedings as oppressive abuse of process.
cases.outcome: Permanent stay of the current conspiracy trial.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria dismissed applications to quash a Commonwealth terrorism indictment against 13 accused, and granted leave for the Crown to amend the indictment for clarity and minor omissions.
cases.outcome: Applications to quash dismissed; Crown given leave to file and serve draft amended indictment.

cases.summary: No-case submission ruling in Benbrika’s terrorism trial concerning count 12, alleging possession of a compact disk connected with preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: The Court decided to hear Benbrika’s no-case submission on count 12 before proceeding further; no final verdict on the count is determined in this ruling.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria refused no-case-to-answer applications on terrorism-possession counts involving the Mansura CD, the Vortex Cookbook, and Al-Battar publications on a computer.
cases.outcome: Directed verdict applications refused; the counts were left to the jury.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria held that alternative verdicts under ss 101.4 and 102.10 of the Criminal Code could not be left to the jury because the Crown had given no notice and the accused had not been afforded procedural fairness.
cases.outcome: No alternative counts were put to the jury; the trial proceeded only on the indictment counts.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria permanently stayed a conspiracy trial against Abdul Nacer Benbrika, Aimen Joud, Fadl Sayadi and Ahmed Raad. The indictment alleged conspiracy to do acts in preparation of a terrorist act, and the judge held the proposed trial would be an abuse of process because of oppression and prior punishment for most of the conduct.
cases.outcome: Permanent stay granted for all accused on abuse-of-process/oppression grounds.

cases.summary: Media sought revocation of suppression orders and access to exhibits in the Benbrika terrorism trial. The court considered linked indictments involving alleged preparation for a terrorist act and alleged support for a terrorist organisation.
cases.outcome: Orders were largely revoked or amended after verdict, with limited exceptions.

cases.summary: The Court refused to exclude evidence the Crown proposed to lead about alleged members of a terrorist organisation and their associations with Sydney men, including a Louth training trip and a 'maximum damage' conversation, as relevant to count 1.
cases.outcome: Application to exclude evidence dismissed; evidence held admissible.

cases.summary: The accused pleaded guilty to preparing/planning a terrorist act. He communicated with a UK contact, conducted internet searches, made a pledge to Islamic State, and prepared for a planned attack to kill a police officer on ANZAC Day 2015. The plot was foiled by police before execution.
cases.outcome: Convicted on plea and sentenced for preparing/planning a terrorist act.

cases.summary: Belal Betka was sentenced for engaging in hostile activity in Syria under s 119.1(2) of the Criminal Code, with a related s 119.2(1) declared-area offence on the schedule. The court found he travelled to Syria in response to Islamic State propaganda, supported Islamic State, and engaged in limited hostile-activity conduct, but was not satisfied he had been in actual combat.
cases.outcome: Sentenced to imprisonment for 3 years and 8 months, with a non-parole period of 2 years and 9 months.

ideology_cause: Islamic opposition to the Syrian government
cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal dismissed the Crown's appeal against sentence for Mehmet Biber's offence of entering Syria with intent to engage in armed hostilities.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; sentence of 4 years and 9 months imprisonment with a 2 years and 6 months non-parole period left undisturbed.
tags: Islamic opposition to the Syrian government

cases.summary: Mehmet Biber was sentenced for entering the Syrian Arab Republic between July and October 2013 with intent to engage in hostile activity/armed hostilities. The court found he travelled with other Australians to join armed groups in Syria and sentenced him to imprisonment.
cases.outcome: Convicted on the indictment and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Judge-alone trial of Cameron Brodie-Hall on two possession counts connected to terrorism/extremist material found in a shared unit in Dudley Park. The court found the prosecution had proved the materials were qualifying, but not possession, and entered not guilty verdicts on both counts.
cases.outcome: Not guilty of Count 1 and Count 2; verdicts entered accordingly.

cases.summary: Bail application for Greg Ceissman, charged with eight counts of breaching an Interim Supervision Order imposed under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The court granted bail.
cases.outcome: Bail granted on conditions.

ideology_cause: support for Islamic State-linked militant ideas
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria sentenced Robert Cerantonio and five co-accused for conduct preparatory to entering the Philippines with intent to engage in hostile activity there, namely encouraging others to overthrow the Southern Philippines government by force or violence.
cases.outcome: Cerantonio was convicted on the offence and sentenced to imprisonment with a non-parole period; forfeiture orders were also made in relation to property, subject to an exception for a copy of the Quran.
tags: support for Islamic State-linked militant ideas

cases.summary: The court considered whether amended particulars were adequate in a joint prosecution alleging conduct preparatory to a covert boat departure from Australia to the Philippines for hostile activity. The judge ruled the particulars inadequate but said they might be capable of further amendment.
cases.outcome: Particulars held inadequate; matter adjourned for possible further amended particulars.

ideology_cause: overthrow by force or violence of the government of the Southern Philippines
cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on whether particulars were adequate and whether the charge was duplex in a prosecution of six accused for conduct preparatory to entering the Philippines with intent to engage in hostile activity there.
cases.outcome: Particulars held adequate; they sufficiently identified conduct capable of connection to the alleged objective; charge not duplex.
tags: overthrow by force or violence of the government of the Southern Philippines

cases.summary: Interlocutory ruling granting certification to appeal a pre-trial decision that the third indictment adequately particularised alleged conduct preparatory to covertly leaving Australia by boat for the Philippines to engage in hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Application for certification granted.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria ruled on the admissibility of evidence in a joint prosecution of six men charged with engaging in conduct preparatory to an offence of entering the Philippines with intent to engage in hostile activity there. The Crown alleged an agreement to prepare to enter the Philippines to encourage or join conduct aimed at overthrowing the southern Philippines government by force or violence.
cases.outcome: On the Crown’s stated basis for admissibility, the challenged evidence of the accuseds’ utterances and actions was held inadmissible or otherwise should not be admitted.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria refused Shayden Thorne’s application for a take-down order and refused the alternative declaration that an existing suppression order required removal of pre-existing online articles. The judgment arose in the context of six men charged with conduct preparatory to entering the Philippines to engage in hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Applications refused; reasons to be suppressed until trial conclusion.

cases.summary: Pre-trial rulings on indictment particulars and construction issues in a six-man prosecution alleging preparation for entry into the Philippines by boat to engage in hostile activity.
cases.outcome: The Court made pre-trial rulings largely upholding the offence theory but requiring several particulars to be confined, deleting surplusage, and adding detail for paragraph (b) objectives.

cases.summary: Ruling in a terrorism trial on whether the accused’s wife could wear a nikab in court; the ruling was made in the context of an alleged conspiracy by three accused to do acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Application to vary the court order was refused; spectators in the public gallery were required to have their faces uncovered.

cases.summary: The offender was sentenced on guilty pleas for two terrorist-association/support offences. One involved repeated association with an Islamic State member and encouragement of his travel to fight with IS; the other involved associations with an IS member and an IS propaganda publisher, including translation, publication and sharing of pro-IS material.
cases.outcome: Convicted on pleas of guilty and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Judgment on media applications for access to trial exhibits in Mustafa Dirani’s terrorism trial. The court refused access to certain exhibits before verdict; the jury later returned a guilty verdict on the conspiracy count.
cases.outcome: Media access to Exhibits E, F and AJ refused; reasons published. Jury returned guilty verdict on the first count.

cases.summary: Pretrial ruling in a terrorism conspiracy prosecution against Mustafa Dirani. The Court admitted extremist material and expert opinion evidence about surveillance/counter-surveillance as probative of the alleged agreement and overt acts in preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Crown evidence of extremist material and CIN 1877 surveillance opinion evidence was admitted; objections under the Evidence Act were rejected.

cases.summary: Sentence after jury verdict for conspiring with Raban Alou and others to do acts in preparation for a terrorist act, connected to the Parramatta shooting plot in October 2015.
cases.outcome: Dirani was sentenced after trial for the conspiracy offence.

cases.summary: EB was sentenced in the NSW Supreme Court for two foreign incursion offences: a 2015 preparatory attempt to leave Australia for Syria, and a 2016 support offence involving assistance to Amin Elmir to cross from Turkey into Syria.
cases.outcome: Imprisonment imposed; the whole sentence ordered to be served as a juvenile offender.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW sentenced Isaac El Matari for preparing terrorist acts in Australia on behalf of Islamic State, preparing to travel via Pakistan to Afghanistan to engage in hostile activity, and knowingly being a member of Islamic State.
cases.outcome: Aggregate sentence imposed for the terrorism and foreign incursion offences, with the membership offence taken into account on the terrorism sentence.

cases.summary: Three accused were convicted after trial of conspiring to do acts in preparation for or planning a terrorist act. The planned terrorist act was an armed attack on the Holsworthy Army Barracks in New South Wales. King J sentenced each to 18 years' imprisonment with a 13 year 6 month non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Each accused convicted and sentenced for the conspiracy to plan a terrorist act.

cases.summary: The court ruled on the admissibility of expert evidence about right-wing extremism in Simon Fleming’s trial for an alleged terrorist act at Windang on 28 November 2021. The evidence of Professor Debra Smith was excluded.
cases.outcome: Professor Smith’s evidence was held inadmissible under s 79 Evidence Act and, alternatively, excluded under s 137.

cases.summary: Costs judgment in a Commonwealth terrorism prosecution arising from Simon Fleming’s conduct at Windang on 28 November 2021. The Court refused to declare the prosecution an abuse of process or award costs, but recommended an ex gratia payment.
cases.outcome: Amended notice of motion dismissed; Court recommended Commonwealth ex gratia payment for reasonable legal costs incurred on and from 13 April 2023.

cases.summary: G, H was charged with four counts of advocating terrorism based on videos uploaded to his Facebook page in late 2015. A jury found the physical elements proved but found him not guilty on mental impairment grounds. The court then ordered detention in safe custody for three years.
cases.outcome: Acquitted by reason of mental impairment on four counts; detained in safe custody for three years under s 20BJ(1).

cases.summary: The appellant was found not guilty by reason of mental impairment on four counts of advocating terrorism based on Facebook videos urging violence against Jewish people, Mahmoud Abbas, Israeli soldiers, and others. The appeal concerned the detention order under s 20BJ of the Crimes Act 1914 (Cth).
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed. The Court held the judge erred in not undertaking a notional sentencing exercise, but that the same or a greater detention period would have been imposed.

cases.summary: Ibrahim Ghazzawy was sentenced for intentionally making a document connected with preparation for a terrorist act, knowing of that connection. The documents formed part of a broader Khalid group terrorist-attack planning matter involving identified targets and coded communications.
cases.outcome: Convicted on plea of guilty and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Daniel Greenfield was sentenced in the District Court of NSW for knowingly collecting or making documents connected with terrorism, after sharing and posting Al Qaeda 'Inspire' magazine issues and a terrorist bomb-design extract online.
cases.outcome: Guilty plea accepted; sentenced to imprisonment for 5 years with a non-parole period of 3 years 9 months.

cases.summary: Fayez Ahmed Hatahet was sentenced after pleading guilty to engaging in hostile activity in Syria between 25 September and 13 December 2012. The court found he entered Syria to look for his brother-in-law, but once there he became an enthusiastic participant supporting the Free Syrian Army and engaged in hostile activities including carrying weapons, carrying a recoilless anti-tank weapon, clearing rubble, encouragement, and one reckless discharge over a wall.
cases.outcome: Convicted on the indictment and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: High Court appeal about whether the sentencing court should have taken the respondent’s likely ineligibility for parole under s 19ALB into account when sentencing for engaging in hostile activity in Syria.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; Court of Criminal Appeal orders set aside; sentence appeal dismissed.

acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: HG was convicted after trial of doing acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The court found he purchased knives, carried disguise items, used extremist propaganda, and was preparing an imminent knife attack.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced after trial.

cases.case_name: R v HG; R v WE (No 1)
cases.summary: Pre-trial evidentiary ruling in a joint prosecution for doing acts in preparation for a terrorist act. The Court ruled on admissibility of statements and other evidence, excluded some admissions made by HG, admitted other evidence, and refused WE's application for a separate trial.
cases.outcome: Some of HG's statements to police were excluded; other challenged evidence was admitted; WE's evidence about Egypt was excluded under s 84; separate trial refused.

cases.case_name: R v HG; R v WE (No 10)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW ruled on the Crown’s late proposed tender of two issues of Islamic State’s Dabiq magazine as evidence against WE in a joint trial. The accused had pleaded not guilty to allegations of acts in preparation for a terrorist act or acts.
cases.outcome: Tender of the two magazine issues rejected as unfairly prejudicial.

cases.case_name: R v HG; R v WE (No 11)
cases.summary: Pre-trial public interest immunity ruling in proceedings against HG and WE, each charged with preparing or planning a terrorist act or acts between 6 and 12 October 2016 in Sydney.
cases.outcome: ASIO’s public interest immunity claim over the disputed material was upheld.

cases.case_name: R v HG; R v We (No 5)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that magazines and footage found on electronic devices linked to HG and WE were admissible as relevant, probative evidence in their trial for doing acts in preparation for a terrorist act or acts.
cases.outcome: Evidence admitted over objection under s 137.

cases.summary: Sentence for intentionally advocating the doing of a terrorist act or the commission of a terrorism offence, based on a prolonged course of right-wing extremist online postings and videos inciting violence against targeted racial and religious groups and a politician.
cases.outcome: Pleaded guilty and sentenced on both counts.

acts_engaged: Court Suppression and Non-publication Orders Act 2010 (NSW)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales considered and granted non-publication orders at Bourhan Hraichie's sentencing hearing. The underlying matter involved guilty pleas to four charges, including acts in preparation for or planning of terrorist acts, and related violent offending.
cases.outcome: Non-publication orders made under s 8(1)(e) Court Suppression and Non-publication Orders Act 2010.

cases.summary: The offender pleaded guilty to a rolled-up Commonwealth terrorism-preparation offence, a NSW threat-to-kill offence, and two NSW assault offences arising from a prison attack on a cellmate. The court imposed a total effective sentence of 34 years with a non-parole period of 29 years.
cases.outcome: Sentenced for four offences; total effective sentence 34 years with 29-year non-parole period.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria decided, before trial, how the jury should be directed on the connection element of six terrorism-possession counts involving Inspire magazines. The court held it was bound to follow Benbrika rather than Khazaal and ruled under s 199.
cases.outcome: Ruling given in favour of the Crown’s requested pre-trial determination procedure being decided by the court, but the substantive construction issue was resolved by adopting Benbrika for the jury direction.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria ruled on admissibility of tendency/context evidence in a single-count terrorism-related prosecution against Adnan Karabegovic for possession of Inspire No. 9 connected with assistance in a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: The court admitted some contextual and state-of-mind evidence, but excluded other categories under s 137 and refused the website-access category (except an SMS exchange).

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on whether the prosecution could use and exhibit other editions of Inspire magazine in a trial for possessing a thing connected with preparation for an act of terrorism.
cases.outcome: Application to exclude evidence was mostly refused, but the Crown was limited in how it could use Inspire issues 1, 2, and parts of 8.

cases.summary: Shane Kent was sentenced after pleading guilty to being a member of the Benbrika terrorist organisation and to making a propaganda document connected with preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Convicted on guilty pleas and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: The court ruled on severance and admissibility in Shane Kent’s terrorism trial. It held counts concerning membership of a terrorist organisation, support for another terrorist organisation, and making a document connected with a terrorist act could be joined, and admitted evidence about al Farooq camp attendance and beheading videos subject to limits.
cases.outcome: Misjoinder challenge failed; no severance ordered; Crown permitted to lead restricted evidence from Witness A and evidence of beheading videos.

ideology_cause: Islamic State of Iraq and Sham
cases.summary: Application for witness identity protection, closed court, AVL, and non-publication orders in a terrorism trial involving alleged preparation for a terrorist attack and alleged travel preparations to join ISIS in Syria.
cases.outcome: Orders made to close court for protected witnesses, take evidence by encrypted AVL, suppress identifying information, and restrict transcript disclosure; the non-publication order was later discharged on 23 November 2017.
tags: Islamic State of Iraq and Sham

cases.summary: The offender pleaded guilty to doing acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act in Sydney in May 2016. The court sentenced him to 19 years' imprisonment with a non-parole period of 14 years and 3 months. The judgment also records admitted conduct attempting to travel to Syria to join ISIS, taken into account on sentence.
cases.outcome: Convicted on plea and sentenced for terrorism planning; foreign incursion conduct taken into account.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling in a Commonwealth terrorism prosecution against Sulayman Khalid. The court held search warrants were invalid for non-compliance with s 3E(5)(d) of the Crimes Act 1914 (Cth), but admitted the seized evidence under s 138 of the Evidence Act 1995 (NSW). It also ruled that SBS Insight footage and YouTube footage of the accused were admissible.
cases.outcome: Motion dismissed; seized evidence and challenged media evidence admitted.

ideology_cause: revenge for Muslims in Iraq and Syria
cases.summary: The offender was convicted and sentenced for engaging in a terrorist act by stabbing Wayne Greenhalgh multiple times at Minto on 10 September 2016, with intent to kill him. The judgment focuses on the attack, its planning, ideological motivation, victim impact, mental illness evidence, and sentence.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced for a terrorist act.
tags: revenge for Muslims in Iraq and Syria

cases.summary: Sentencing of Arsalan Khawaja for making a false Border Watch report about M1’s alleged extremist conduct, and for creating forged notebook entries falsely depicting Mr Nizamdeen as preparing for terrorist acts and then misleading police, plus an admitted witness-interference offence.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced on an aggregate basis.

cases.summary: Bail application by Mahmoud Khayat, charged with conspiring to do acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act. The court refused bail under s 15AA of the Crimes Act.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

cases.summary: Sentencing of two brothers for conspiring to do acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act involving a bomb hidden in a meat grinder placed in luggage on an Etihad flight.
cases.outcome: Imprisonment imposed for terrorism offences arising from the failed aircraft-bomb plot.

acts_engaged: Court Suppression and Non-publication Orders Act 2010 (NSW)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted suppression orders and partial closed-court orders to protect sensitive evidence in terrorism proceedings against Khaled and Mahmoud Khayat.
cases.outcome: Orders 1–19 were made, including suppression, redaction, access restrictions, and closure of court during evidence from three witnesses.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on whether recorded interviews of Khaled Khayat were admissible in a terrorism conspiracy prosecution. The Court rejected challenges based on alleged inducement, invalid extension of the investigation period, and unlawful detention, and admitted the interviews.
cases.outcome: Recorded interviews admitted into evidence.

cases.summary: Mahmoud Khayat sought a separate trial from co-accused Khaled Khayat on a conspiracy charge alleging acts in preparation for a terrorist act between January and July 2017. The Court refused the application.
cases.outcome: Application for a separate trial refused.

cases.summary: Pre-trial evidentiary ruling in a terrorism conspiracy prosecution against Mahmoud Khayat and Khaled Khayat concerning alleged preparation for a terrorist act using an improvised explosive device or chemical dispersal device.
cases.outcome: The Court held that three statements were capable of amounting to lies and could be used by the Crown as consciousness-of-guilt evidence; one statement could not.

cases.summary: Khazaal was sentenced after a jury conviction for making a document connected with assistance in a terrorist act. The document was a compiled Arabic book promoting assassination and violent jihad, submitted for publication online.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced for making a document connected with assistance in a terrorist act.

cases.summary: High Court consideration of whether the respondent, convicted of making a document connected with assistance in a terrorist act, could rely on the s 101.5(5) defence.
cases.outcome: The excerpt only notes that the High Court considered the defence issue; it does not provide the substantive disposition.

cases.summary: High Court appeal in a terrorism-document case. The Court allowed the Crown appeal, restored Khazaal’s conviction on count 1, and remitted sentence for reconsideration.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; conviction on count 1 restored; sentence appeal remitted.

cases.summary: Bail review in a terrorism-document prosecution. The court considered the strength of the Crown case, the seriousness of the alleged conduct, and whether bail should continue on conditions.
cases.outcome: Bail granted and continued on existing terms over the adjournment.

cases.summary: Court of Appeal sentence appeal by Agim Kruezi arising from guilty pleas to count 1 (preparations for incursions into a foreign State) and count 3 (acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act). The appeal challenged the sentence structure and non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Application for leave to appeal refused.

cases.summary: The offender pleaded guilty to a rolled-up count of planning/preparation for a terrorist act, comprising two particulars: one involving recruitment/scouting of Corrective Services NSW officers for potential violent attack, and one involving support for Isaac El Matari’s plan for an extremist Islamic insurgency. An earlier terrorism-advocacy offence was also taken into account at sentence.
cases.outcome: Imprisonment for 6 years with a non-parole period of 4 years and 6 months; sentence backdated to 23 May 2021.

acts_engaged: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth) Division 102 — proscription regime
cases.summary: Crown appeal against sentence for membership of the PKK. The Court of Criminal Appeal held the sentencing judge erred by taking account of the PKK’s perceived merits and ideology, but dismissed the appeal and left the Community Correction Order in place.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; sentence not disturbed.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling during a jury trial on the meaning of 'engaging in armed hostilities' and the directions to be given on a foreign-fighting charge against Renas Lelikan. The jury ultimately could not reach a verdict and was discharged.
cases.outcome: Ruling adopted the accused's proposed construction in substance, requiring a realistic connection between the acts alleged and the objective of engaging in armed hostilities. Trial ended in a hung jury.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW sentenced Renas Lelikan for membership of the PKK as a terrorist organisation. The court found his conduct was informal membership involving travel with HPG guerrillas, wearing uniforms and insignia, carrying weapons, and publishing supportive writing, but characterised it as low in seriousness and imposed a community correction order.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced to a community correction order instead of imprisonment.

cases.summary: Pretrial motion on whether terrorism counts in the indictment were duplicitous. The Court held the counts were not duplicitous (subject to amendment of count 2) and adjourned the motion.
cases.outcome: Motion adjourned; Court indicated counts 2, 3 and 4 were not bad for duplicity, subject to amendment of count 2.

acts_engaged: National Security Information (Criminal and Civil Proceedings) Act 2004 (Cth)
cases.summary: Constitutional challenge to the National Security Information (Criminal and Civil Proceedings) Act 2004 in Lodhi’s terrorism prosecution; the Court upheld Pt 3 and dismissed the motion.
cases.outcome: Notice of Motion dismissed; Pt 3 of the Act held valid.

cases.summary: The court considered and dismissed a defence motion challenging duplicity and particulars in an indictment charging Faheem Khalid Lodhi with terrorism-preparation offences arising from alleged conduct in Sydney in October 2003.
cases.outcome: Motion dismissed; pre-trial ruling upheld the indictment, subject to possible amendment by the Crown.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales considered and granted the Crown’s application for overseas witnesses to give evidence by audio visual link in Faheem Khalid Lodhi’s terrorism prosecution.
cases.outcome: Application for AVL evidence allowed for three witnesses, limited initially to pre-trial applications, with an observer to be arranged.

cases.summary: The Court considered whether to make closed-court, non-publication, pseudonym and screening orders for an upcoming terrorism trial against Faheem Khalid Lodhi involving alleged preparatory acts connected to a terrorist plot in Sydney in October 2003.
cases.outcome: Protective orders were made in favour of the Commonwealth Attorney-General, including closed court and non-publication orders for specified ASIO evidence and a screening order for certain ASIO witnesses.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW refused to require Izhar Ul-Haque to give evidence at Faheem Lodhi’s trial, accepting that his evidence may incriminate him under foreign law and that the interests of justice did not require compulsion.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; witness not required to give evidence.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling refusing to quash a fresh indictment charging Faheem Khalid Lodhi with preparatory terrorist-offence counts arising from alleged October 2003 conduct in Sydney.
cases.outcome: Application to quash the new indictment refused; indictment allowed to stand in amended form.

cases.summary: The court refused the accused’s application for directed verdicts on four terrorism-preparation counts arising from alleged conduct in Sydney in October 2003, including collecting maps, seeking explosive materials information, making aerial photographs, and possessing a document about poisons and explosives.
cases.outcome: Application for directed verdicts refused.

cases.summary: Faheem Khalid Lodhi was sentenced after jury verdicts on three terrorism-preparation counts arising from a single interrupted plot to bomb part of the Australian electricity supply system and to assemble an explosive device. A fourth aerial-photograph count was acquitted.
cases.outcome: Convicted on counts 1, 2 and 3; acquitted on count 4; sentenced to 20 years on count 2 and 10 years each on counts 1 and 3, all concurrent, with a 15-year non-parole period.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW ruled on whether, in a terrorism-preparation prosecution, the jury had to be unanimous not only about two preparatory acts but also about the category of intended target. The court held unanimity was required as to two acts, but not as to the specific target category.
cases.outcome: Accused’s proposed extended unanimity direction was allowed in part only.

cases.summary: Sentencing of Zaky Mallah for recklessly making a threat to cause serious harm to a Commonwealth public official, after a trial in which he was acquitted of two terrorism-preparation counts arising from the same broader course of conduct.
cases.outcome: Imprisonment imposed for the threat offence, with recognisance release conditions.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court considered and dismissed the accused’s motion to exclude undercover-recorded conversations and items obtained in a controlled operation. The ruling held the evidence admissible despite impropriety arguments.
cases.outcome: Motion of accused dismissed; evidence admitted.

cases.summary: Mr Biber was sentenced after pleading guilty to intentionally contravening a control order in force against him between October 2021 and April 2022. The court found he knowingly engaged in business activities without notifying the AFP as required by control 9 and imposed a community corrections order.
cases.outcome: Convicted on a guilty plea and sentenced to a 2-year community corrections order.

cases.summary: The accused pleaded guilty to preparing for or planning a terrorist act after acquiring materials and partially constructing IEDs intended for detonation in Melbourne. Police intervention stopped completion and execution.
cases.outcome: Sentenced to 7 years' imprisonment for preparation/planning a terrorist act, with a non-parole period of 5 years and 3 months.

cases.summary: Milad Atai was sentenced for aiding and abetting the terrorist act in which Curtis Cheng was murdered, two counts of intentionally collecting funds for Islamic State, and had a terrorist-organisation membership offence taken into account on sentence.
cases.outcome: Convicted on guilty pleas; sentenced to an aggregate term of 38 years with a 28 years 6 months non-parole period.

cases.summary: The District Court corrected a January 2016 sentence imposed for contravening a control order under s 104.27 of the Criminal Code, because the original sentence lacked the required non-parole period for a terrorism offence.
cases.outcome: Sentence quashed and replaced to comply with the statutory non-parole-period requirement.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling in a prosecution for three preparatory offences under s 7 of the Crimes (Foreign Incursions and Recruitments) Act 1978 (Cth), said to be preparatory to entering Syria to engage in hostile activities.
cases.outcome: Lasry J ruled that the relevant fault element under s 7(1)(a) is intention; declined to determine the scope of 'engaging in armed hostilities' beyond what was necessary; and held that s 7(1B) does not impose an evidential burden under s 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.

cases.summary: The accused were sentenced for attempting to engage in a terrorist act on 25 November 2016 and engaging in a terrorist act on 11 December 2016 by setting fire to the Imam Ali Islamic Centre mosque in Fawkner.
cases.outcome: Mohamed and Chaarani each sentenced to 22 years' imprisonment with a 17-year non-parole period; Moukhaiber sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment with a 12-year non-parole period.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on relevance of evidence in a terrorism prosecution over two mosque fire incidents at the Imam Ali Islamic Centre, Fawkner: an attempted fire-setting on 25 November 2016 and a completed arson on 11 December 2016.
cases.outcome: The Court held the impugned evidence relevant and allowed it to be led, subject to any later admissibility ruling.

cases.summary: Pre-trial subpoena ruling in a terrorism case arising from the alleged arson destruction of a mosque and an earlier alleged attempt to destroy the same mosque.
cases.outcome: Application to set aside subpoenas refused; legitimate forensic purpose found.

cases.summary: The court ruled on the admissibility of mobile-phone evidence in the prosecution of three accused for an attempted burning of the Imam Ali Islamic Centre on 25 November 2016 and a completed burning on 11 December 2016, alleged to be terrorist acts aimed at intimidating the Shia Muslim community.
cases.outcome: Most challenged phone material was admitted; the Man Monis article was excluded.

cases.summary: The Court ruled that admissions made by counsel for one accused during a defence response could be used only against that accused, not the co-accused, in a joint terrorism trial arising from two mosque arson incidents in Fawkner.
cases.outcome: Admissions made by Chaarani’s counsel were admissible against Chaarani only and could not be used against Mohamed or Moukhaiber.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of Victoria ruled that arson and attempted arson could not be left to the jury as alternative verdicts to the charged terrorist offences, and in any event would not be left in the interests of justice.
cases.outcome: Alternative verdict applications refused.

cases.summary: Mirsad Mulahalilovic was sentenced after pleading guilty to possessing firearm ammunition at Sydney on or about 19 August 2005, recklessly as to its connection with preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Convicted on the single count and sentenced to imprisonment.

ideology_cause: support for armed hostilities in Syria
cases.summary: Muhammad Abdul-Karim Musleh pleaded guilty to performing services for others to support or promote their entry into Syria to engage in armed hostilities. The Court sentenced him to imprisonment and made a recognizance release order.
cases.outcome: Convicted on the indictment count; sentenced to 2 years and 1 month imprisonment with a recognizance release order after 1 year.
tags: support for armed hostilities in Syria

cases.summary: Bail application by Ahmad Naizmand, charged with five offences alleging breach of a Federal Court control order by accessing proscribed online material linked to terrorism and Islamic State. Bail was refused because exceptional circumstances were not shown.
cases.outcome: Application for bail refused; no exceptional circumstances established under s 15AA Crimes Act 1914.

cases.summary: The offender pleaded guilty to five counts of contravening a control order by accessing Islamic State and Jabhat al-Nusra propaganda videos on YouTube over February 2016. The court convicted him and imposed imprisonment.
cases.outcome: Convicted on all five counts; single non-parole period and head sentence imposed.

cases.summary: Bail application for a defendant charged with multiple contraventions and attempted contraventions of a terrorism-related control order. The Court found no exceptional circumstances and refused bail.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

ideology_cause: terroristic language alleged by Crown but not accepted as terrorism offence
cases.summary: Mert Ney was sentenced after pleading guilty to murder of Michaela Dunn and wounding Lin Bo with intent to cause grievous bodily harm arising from a knife attack and violent rampage in Sydney on 13 August 2019.
cases.outcome: Aggregate sentence imposed; life imprisonment refused.
tags: terroristic language alleged by Crown but not accepted as terrorism offence

cases.summary: Bail application for a 16-year-old charged with collecting funds for Islamic State between 21 and 22 March 2016 in New South Wales.
cases.outcome: Bail granted on strict conditions after the court found exceptional circumstances and no unacceptable risk could not be managed by conditions.

cases.summary: Wayne O’Brien and Shannon Hudson pleaded guilty to intentionally causing serious injury to Minh Duong in a prolonged, unprovoked racist assault in Ascot Vale on 27 June 2012. The court found partial racial motivation and sentenced both offenders.
cases.outcome: Both offenders were convicted and sentenced after guilty pleas.

cases.summary: Sentencing of Omarjan Azari for a funding offence involving Islamic State and a planning offence involving a domestic terrorist attack discussion with Mohammad Ali Baryalei.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced for terrorism offences.

cases.summary: On a defence application, the Supreme Court discharged the jury in Omarjan Azari’s terrorism trial because extensive publicity about related committal proceedings created a real risk of unfair prejudice. The underlying charge was that Azari did an act in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act on 15 September 2014.
cases.outcome: Application to discharge the jury granted.

cases.summary: Sentence for possessing a knife connected with preparation for a terrorist act and for threatening a judicial officer during a bail hearing.
cases.outcome: Convicted on both charges and sentenced to imprisonment.

cases.summary: Full Court reference answering questions about whether statutory immunity under s 148B of the Police Administration Act could apply to Zachary Rolfe’s shooting of Kumanjayi Wilson during an arrest at Yuendumu.
cases.outcome: Reference answered in favour of the defence on the availability of s 148B and its coexistence with s 208E.

cases.summary: Sharrouf was sentenced after pleading guilty to possessing six clocks and 140 batteries knowing they were connected with preparation for a terrorist act. The court accepted he was mentally ill but treated the offence as serious terrorism conduct and imposed imprisonment with a non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Convicted on guilty plea and sentenced.

cases.summary: Momena Shoma was sentenced for intentionally engaging in a terrorist act after stabbing Roger Singaravelu in the neck in his home in Melbourne on 9 February 2018. The court found the attack was planned, ideologically motivated, and intended to advance Islamic State-inspired violent jihad and intimidate government or the public.
cases.outcome: Convicted on plea of guilty and sentenced for intentionally engaging in a terrorist act.

cases.summary: The accused pleaded guilty to a prison terrorist attack on Kailee Mitz and to membership of Islamic State. The Court sentenced her to 12 years for the terrorist act and 2 years concurrently for membership, with a new aggregate head sentence and non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Convicted on both charges and sentenced after guilty pleas.

ideology_cause: support for opposition forces against the Assad regime
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: Court of Appeal decision on competing sentence appeals by Omar Succarieh and the Commonwealth concerning four CFIRA offences: two counts of preparing for incursions into Syria and two counts of giving money to support hostile activity there.
cases.outcome: Both the offender’s leave application and the Crown appeal were dismissed; the original sentences were upheld.
tags: support for opposition forces against the Assad regime

cases.summary: Sentencing for Talal Alameddine’s guilty pleas to intentionally possessing a revolver connected with preparation for a terrorist act and supplying that revolver to Raban Alou, who passed it to Farhad Jabar Khalil Mohammad for the 2 October 2015 Parramatta attack on Curtis Cheng.
cases.outcome: Convicted on both counts and sentenced to substantial imprisonment with accumulation between the Commonwealth and State sentences.

cases.summary: The Court ruled on a defence subpoena seeking material about NSW and AFP controlled operations used in the investigation of Taleb’s alleged terrorism conduct. Some paragraphs were struck out, and some production was ordered subject to public interest immunity claims.
cases.outcome: Substantially allowed and dismissed in part: several subpoena paragraphs were struck out; limited production ordered for controlled-operation materials; some requests set aside.

cases.summary: Pre-trial voir dire on admissibility and validity of evidence in a prosecution for doing acts preparatory to engaging in hostile activity in a foreign country.
cases.outcome: Most challenged evidence was admitted, but the ERISP interview was excluded. The controlled-operation evidence, telephone intercepts, and limited phone/Facebook material were ruled admissible.
