ideology_cause: foreign incursion/joining the war in Syria
cases.summary: The Court revoked Moudasser Taleb’s recognizance order after admitted breaches between November 2020 and April 2021, and imposed a 3-year Community Corrections Order with supervision, treatment, and de-radicalisation conditions.
cases.outcome: Breach of recognizance established; recognizance revoked; 3-year Community Corrections Order imposed.
tags: foreign incursion/joining the war in Syria

cases.summary: The Supreme Court ruled on admissibility of defence expert evidence from Keysar Trad. Evidence about Islam was admitted, but evidence about the conflict in Syria and Islamic State practices was excluded.
cases.outcome: Partial admission of Mr Trad’s evidence; exclusion of evidence concerning the conflict in Syria and Islamic State practices.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted the prosecution leave to amend the indictment against Moudasser Taleb during trial, changing the fault element for the preparatory foreign-incursion charge from recklessness to intention. The ruling did not determine guilt; it addressed the form of the charge in a case in which the accused was later found guilty by a jury.
cases.outcome: Application to amend the indictment granted.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling on the legal directions and evidentiary issues in Mr Taleb’s trial for conduct preparatory to a foreign incursion offence.
cases.outcome: Application for directed verdict of acquittal dismissed; jury directions resolved on unanimity, fault element, consciousness of guilt, and entrapment.

cases.summary: Moudasser Taleb was sentenced for engaging in conduct preparatory to committing a foreign incursion offence. The Court found he engaged in a two-month course of preparatory acts in 2017, but imposed a recognizance release order rather than imprisonment.
cases.outcome: Convicted; released without passing sentence on a 5-year recognizance with 2 years of supervision and conditions.

cases.summary: The Victorian Court of Appeal allowed Jack Thomas’s appeal against conviction. It held that his 8 March 2003 AFP interview in Pakistan was not voluntary and should have been excluded, because he was under coercive pressure and denied legal access contrary to s 23G of the Crimes Act. The convictions for receiving funds from a terrorist organisation and possessing a falsified Australian passport were quashed.
cases.outcome: Appeal against conviction allowed; convictions quashed; verdicts of acquittal directed.

cases.summary: Appeal against conviction after the appellant was convicted of intentionally receiving funds from a terrorist organisation and possessing a falsified Australian passport. The Court considered whether fresh evidence justified a retrial and ordered one.
cases.outcome: Convictions quashed; retrial ordered.

cases.summary: Appeal application seeking to rescind a retrial order after convictions for receiving funds from a terrorist organisation and possessing a falsified passport were quashed.
cases.outcome: Application refused; the retrial order stood.

cases.summary: Mazen Touma pleaded guilty to four terrorism-related counts arising from a single continuing course of conduct: acquiring ammunition, attempting to make improvised explosive devices, and possessing materials and extremist media connected with preparation for a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Convicted on all four counts and sentenced to concurrent imprisonment terms, with a single non-parole period.

cases.summary: Adams J determined a voir dire on whether records of interview with ASIO and AFP were admissible in a prosecution alleging that Izhar Ul-Haque received terrorist-training from Lashkar-e-Taiba in Pakistan.
cases.outcome: The records of interview of 7 and 12 November 2003 and 9 January 2004 were ruled inadmissible.

cases.summary: Youssef Uweinat pleaded guilty to being a member of Islamic State and to intentionally advocating terrorist acts and terrorism offences over a five-month period in 2019. The court sentenced him to imprisonment and imposed a non-parole period.
cases.outcome: Convicted on both counts and sentenced to 3 years 11 months total effective imprisonment, with a 2 years 11 months non-parole period.

acts_engaged: Charter of the United Nations Act 1945 (Cth)
cases.summary: Pretrial ruling on whether expert evidence about the LTTE’s structure and organisation was admissible in a terrorism prosecution of three accused for LTTE membership, funding and support offences.
cases.outcome: Dr Chalk’s evidence was ruled inadmissible; Dr Smith’s evidence was generally admissible, subject to reduction to statement form and further testing.

cases.summary: Bail application pending retrial for an alleged terrorist act preparation/planning offence. The applicant had been tried, the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict, and the Court refused release pending retrial.
cases.outcome: Application for release refused.

cases.summary: Bellew J ruled on a defence challenge to the admissibility of two religious publications seized from the accused while on remand. The Court held the publications were not relevant and, if relevant, would have been excluded under s 137. The underlying prosecution alleged that WE and HG planned a terrorist act in Sydney between 6 and 12 October 2016 involving bladed weapons and attacks on law enforcement officers or the public.
cases.outcome: Evidence of the accused’s possession of the two publications was excluded.

cases.summary: Pre-trial ruling in a terrorism prosecution about whether the accused could adduce large volumes of non-extremist electronic material; the Court excluded the evidence as having low probative value and risking undue waste of time.
cases.outcome: Application to tender the material was refused; evidence excluded.

cases.summary: WE was found guilty by a jury of jointly doing acts in preparation for, or planning, a terrorist act with HG between 6 and 12 October 2016 in Sydney. The court sentenced him for this terrorism offence after finding the planned knife attack was imminent and motivated by extremist ideology.
cases.outcome: Convicted and sentenced for a federal terrorism-preparation offence.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW excluded parts of the Crown’s late-served expert report in a terrorist-plot trial because the accused could not fairly meet it with responsive expert evidence.
cases.outcome: Application to exclude evidence granted; parts of the expert report were excluded under s 137.

cases.summary: Bail application by a youth charged with preparing for a terrorist act or acts. The Court found exceptional circumstances due to delay, but refused bail because unacceptable risks of flight and further offending remained.
cases.outcome: Application for release refused.

cases.case_name: Raad v Director of Public Prosecutions
cases.summary: Bail application by Ezzit Raad, who had been charged with two terrorism offences and was awaiting a jury trial; the court refused bail because exceptional circumstances were not shown.
cases.outcome: Application for bail dismissed.

cases.summary: Coronial finding into Ahmad Numan Haider’s death after he attacked two police officers outside Endeavour Hills Police Station on 23 September 2014.
cases.outcome: The coroner found Haider died from a gunshot wound fired by Officer A after Haider stabbed Officers A and B. No adverse finding was made against the officers.

cases.case_name: Re Inquest into the Death of: KAI HAO  BC202320387
cases.summary: Coronial inquest into Kai Hao’s death arising from the Brighton Siege incident, including the fatal shotgun shooting, hostage-taking, and bomb threats made by Yacub Khayre.
cases.outcome: Coroner found Kai Hao died from shotgun wounds inflicted by Yacub Khayre, but could not make a definitive finding that the conduct was motivated by extremist ideology or tantamount to a terror attack.

cases.case_name: Re Inquest into the death of: YACUB KHAYRE BC202320399
cases.summary: Coronial inquest into the death of Yacub Khayre following the Brighton Siege incident at the Buckingham International Serviced Apartments on 5 June 2017, including findings on cause of death and whether his conduct was extremist or terror-related.
cases.outcome: The coroner found Khayre died from multiple gunshot wounds and that police response was reasonable. No definitive finding was made that his conduct was a terror attack or motivated by extremist ideology.

cases.case_name: Re RE SESTILIO MALASPINA AND HASSAN KHALIF SHIRE ALI BC202120444
cases.summary: Coronial inquest into the deaths of Sestilio Malaspina and Hassan Khalif Shire Ali arising from the 9 November 2018 Bourke Street attack, including findings on terrorism, police response, and counter-terrorism management.
cases.outcome: The Coroner found Hassan’s actions on 9 November 2018 were a premeditated ISIS-inspired terrorist attack; confirmed Sestilio Malaspina was killed by Hassan; and found the police shooting of Hassan was justified.

cases.summary: Federal Court application by the AFP for an interim control order against Alo-Bridget Namoa, based on her prior conviction for conspiring to prepare or plan a terrorist act and alleged ongoing risk factors.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made.

cases.summary: The Court confirmed, without variation, an interim control order made against Alo-Bridget Namoa under s 104.4 of the Criminal Code. The respondent did not oppose confirmation and the Court was satisfied the statutory preconditions were met, including that she had been convicted in Australia of an offence relating to terrorism or a terrorist act.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation.

cases.case_name: RZBV and Director-General of Security, Minister for Foreign Affairs, Re
ideology_cause: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The AAT reviewed and affirmed ASIO’s adverse security assessment and the Minister’s cancellation of the applicant’s passport. The assessment was that he likely intended to travel to Syria to engage in politically motivated violence or support ISIL, and would be a threat to Australia and foreign countries if allowed to travel.
cases.outcome: Assessment and passport cancellation affirmed.
tags: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)

cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal allowed a sentence appeal and re-sentenced the applicant for making documents connected with preparation for a terrorist act. The court held the original sentence failed to account for the utilitarian value of the guilty plea.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; original sentence quashed; applicant re-sentenced.

cases.case_name: Save Children Australia v Minister for Home Affairs
cases.summary: Save the Children Australia sought habeas corpus and judicial review relief concerning the Commonwealth’s alleged ability or failure to secure repatriation of Australian women and children detained in Al-Roj camp, Syria. The Court refused the application, finding the respondents did not control the detention and that no decision not to repatriate had been proven.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed.

cases.case_name: SDCV and Director-General of Security, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The Tribunal reviewed an ASIO adverse security assessment and affirmed it. ASIO assessed the applicant as a risk to security because of his support for politically motivated violence and ISIL, including use of a covert phone, encrypted communications, and transmission of a pro-ISIL sermon.
cases.outcome: Reviewable decision affirmed; the adverse security assessment was upheld.

acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: Full Court appeal from an AAT decision affirming an adverse security assessment made by the Director-General of Security against SDCV. The assessment was based on support for politically motivated violence and ISIL, and on communications security tradecraft with security-concern individuals.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; s 46(2) of the AAT Act held valid; costs ordered against the applicant.

ideology_cause: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)
cases.summary: High Court appeal about whether secrecy provisions in the AAT Act were constitutionally valid in a merits-review appeal from an ASIO adverse security assessment and visa cancellation decision.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed by majority; s 46(2) held valid.
tags: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)

cases.summary: Bail application by Thomas Sewell in respect of charges arising from alleged violence on 9 August 2025 and 31 August 2025; bail granted subject to strict conditions.
cases.outcome: Bail granted.

cases.summary: Appeal from convictions for hindering a territory public official and hindering Commonwealth public officials arising from police efforts to cordon off Parliament House during a sword incident.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; convictions and sentences set aside; verdicts of not guilty entered on both hindering charges.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Avakian (No 2)
acts_engaged: Court Suppression and Non-publication Orders Act 2010 (NSW)
cases.summary: The State sought a non-publication order to prevent identification of High Risk Offenders Assessment Committee members in minutes used in opposition to an Interim Supervision Order application. The Court refused the order, lifted an interim restriction, and ordered the plaintiff to pay costs.
cases.outcome: Notice of motion dismissed; interim publication restriction lifted; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Barez (Final)
cases.summary: The State applied for an extended supervision order against Edris Barez. The Court found he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if not supervised and confirmed an ESO for one year with conditions.
cases.outcome: ESO granted and confirmed.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Benshabir (Interlocutory)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court heard the State’s urgent application for an interim supervision order against Benshabir under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court held that the District Court’s sentence orders had taken effect, so Benshabir was not presently an eligible offender and the Court lacked power to make the order. The application was dismissed.
cases.outcome: Application for an interim supervision order dismissed; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Benshabir (Interlocutory) (No 2)
cases.summary: The State sought an extended supervision order against Mr Yaqoob Benshabir under the THRO Act. After a District Court sentence appeal reduced his custody status, the Supreme Court held he was no longer an eligible offender and dismissed the summons, setting aside the expert-appointment order.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed; interlocutory order under s 24(5) set aside; costs awarded to the defendant.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Benshabir (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The State of New South Wales sought an extended supervision order against Yaqoob Benshabir. The Court ordered expert examinations under s 24(5) but refused an interim supervision order under s 27 because it was not satisfied his custody would expire before determination.
cases.outcome: Expert examinations ordered; interim supervision order refused.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v BP (No 2)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW confirmed and finalised conditions for an interim supervision order against BP under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), requiring compliance with extensive supervision, monitoring, search, internet, association, and treatment conditions.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made for 28 days with prescribed and additional conditions.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v BP (Preliminary)
acts_engaged: Court Suppression and Non-publication Orders Act 2010 (NSW)
cases.summary: Preliminary hearing on the State of New South Wales’ application against BP for an extended supervision order, interim supervision order, and examination orders under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court found the statutory preconditions for examination orders were met and listed the matter for further submissions on an interim supervision order.
cases.outcome: Examination orders made; interim access restrictions and pseudonym order made; matter listed for further submissions on interim supervision order.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Ceissman
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW varied Greg Ceissman’s extended supervision order, accepting most proposed conditions but refusing one proposed accommodation condition and ordering the amended ESO conditions to apply.
cases.outcome: Application to vary the ESO granted in part and refused in part.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Ceissman (No 2)
cases.summary: The Court considered NSW's application under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW) and ordered an Extended Supervision Order against Greg Ceissman after finding he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence.
cases.outcome: Extended Supervision Order granted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Cheema (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW refused a permanent stay, held Ahsan Kamal Cheema to be a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender, and made orders for psychiatric and psychological examination plus a 28-day interim supervision order with conditions.
cases.outcome: Stay dismissed; defendant held to be a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender; examination orders and interim supervision order made.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Church (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW considered and dismissed the State’s application for a 12-month extended supervision order against Mr Church under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court accepted some past social-media advocacy and associations with violent extremism but was not satisfied to a high degree of probability that he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Application for an extended supervision order dismissed; interim supervision order dissolved.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Church (Preliminary)
cases.summary: Preliminary hearing on the State’s application for an Interim Supervision Order and later Extended Supervision Order against Mr Church under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), based on alleged Salafi-jihadi violent extremist conduct and risk of future terrorism offending.
cases.outcome: The Court found the statutory conditions for an interim supervision order were met and made orders for psychiatric/psychological examinations, plus an Interim Supervision Order for 28 days from 19 March 2021, subject to specified conditions.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Cornish
cases.summary: The State sought leave to discontinue proceedings brought under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 against Matthew David Cornish. The Court granted leave to discontinue, but conditioned it on payment of costs and a requirement that the plaintiff not reapply for orders without leave of the Court.
cases.outcome: Leave to discontinue granted with conditions.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Desmond Liddington (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted the State’s preliminary application for an interim supervision order against Desmond Liddington under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017, together with orders for psychiatric and psychological examinations.
cases.outcome: Application allowed; interim supervision order made for 28 days from 3 February 2025 and examination orders made.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Dickson (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted the State's application for an interim supervision order against George Dickson, a convicted NSW underlying terrorism offender, after finding the material capable of showing an unacceptable risk of serious terrorism offending.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order granted; psychiatric and psychological examinations ordered; court file access restricted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Dunn
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted the State’s application under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. Dunn was found to pose an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence, and the Court ordered nine months’ continued detention followed by three years’ extended supervision.
cases.outcome: Application granted; CDO and ESO made.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Dunn (A Pseudonym)
cases.summary: The State sought a continuing detention order under the THRO Act against Dunn, and the Court made interim orders appointing two psychiatrists and imposing an interim detention order. The Court held the supporting material, if proved, would justify a CDO or ESO because Dunn had made statements advocating support for terrorist acts and posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence.
cases.outcome: Interim detention order granted; two psychiatrists appointed to examine the defendant.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Elmir
cases.summary: The State of New South Wales sought an interim supervision order under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 NSW for Amin Elmir, relying on his guilty plea to a Commonwealth foreign-incursion preparation offence and related terrorism-risk material. The Court granted the interim supervision order and ordered expert examinations, with timing deferred until after his criminal sentencing.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order granted; orders made for expert examinations and short minutes of order.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Elmir
cases.summary: The Supreme Court considered, at a preliminary hearing, whether the State had shown that matters in the supporting materials would justify a further extended supervision order against Mr Elmir. The Court held it was not so satisfied and dismissed the application.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; costs ordered against the State.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Elomar (Final)
cases.summary: The State sought a further two-year extended supervision order against Ahmed Elomar. The Court found the formal prerequisites were met but was not satisfied to a high degree of probability that he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence, so the application was dismissed and the interim supervision order revoked.
cases.outcome: Application for an extended supervision order dismissed; interim supervision order revoked.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Elomar (Preliminary)
cases.summary: Final hearing on the State of New South Wales’ application for an extended supervision order in relation to Ahmed Elomar. The Court extended an interim supervision order until 23 April 2021 pending final determination.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made/extended pending final judgment on the ESO application.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Farhat
cases.summary: NSW applied under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 for an extended supervision order and interim supervision order against Mohommed Farhat after his conviction for property damage and arson offences committed in November 2024. The Court appointed experts and refused interim supervision, while finding the material could justify a final supervision order.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order refused; experts appointed for final hearing; access to file restricted; matter listed for further directions.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Farhat (final)
cases.summary: The State sought an extended supervision order against Mohammed Farhat after his imprisonment for property damage and arson offences involving anti-Israel slogans and a Hezbollah tattoo. Fagan J held the defendant did not pose an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence and dismissed the application.
cases.outcome: Application for an extended supervision order dismissed; costs ordered against the State.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Fayad (Final)
cases.summary: The State sought and obtained a two-year extended supervision order against Wassim Fayad after the Court found, to a high degree of probability, that he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: ESO granted for two years, with supervision conditions continued and a timetable set for any variation application.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Fayad (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The State sought a preliminary THRO Act order against Wassim Fayad. The Court found the statutory criteria met and ordered psychiatric/psychological examinations plus a 28-day interim supervision order with conditions.
cases.outcome: Application granted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Fayad (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The State sought a further interim supervision order and expert examinations for Wassim Fayad under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The Court held it was not satisfied the material, if proved, would justify an Extended Supervision Order and dismissed the applications.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Fayad (Variation of Conditions)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court varied the conditions of an extended supervision order imposed on Wassim Fayad, adjusting several reporting, internet, association, extremism, travel and accommodation conditions while leaving most conditions in place.
cases.outcome: Leave granted to file an amended notice of motion; the prior order of 27 February 2021 was revoked; the ESO conditions were varied as set out in the schedule; otherwise the motion was dismissed; costs were ordered separately.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Gavin
cases.summary: The State of New South Wales sought interlocutory disclosure relief in connection with its application for a 3-year Extended Supervision Order against Mr Gavin under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The court held certain confidential material was not relevant to the proceedings and could be withheld/redacted.
cases.outcome: Disclosure relief granted; confidential material held irrelevant to the supervision-order proceedings and redactions/sealing ordered.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Gavin
cases.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed the State’s application for an interim/extended supervision order against Mr Gavin. Harrison J found Gavin was an eligible offender but was not a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender and was not shown to pose an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed with costs.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v GB by his Tutor
cases.summary: The State sought an interim supervision order and extended supervision order against GB. The Court held the allegations, even if proved, did not justify an ESO because the evidence did not establish a high degree of probability of an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Haidar
cases.summary: The State sought interim and then extended supervision orders against Haidar as a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender. The Court held the State had not shown he advocated support for any terrorist act or violent extremism and dismissed the summons.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; costs ordered against the plaintiff.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Hardy
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made an interim supervision order against Christopher Bruce Hardy for 28 days, and ordered psychiatric and psychological examinations, pending the extended supervision order proceedings. The judgment discusses Hardy’s earlier threatening letter, weapons possession, and blueprint-related conduct as the basis for risk assessment.
cases.outcome: Interim Supervision Order granted with conditions modified from those sought by the State.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Hardy (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW ordered Christopher Bruce Hardy to be subject to an extended supervision order for 18 months under the THRO Act after finding he was a convicted NSW terrorism activity offender and posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence.
cases.outcome: ESO granted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW adjourned the State’s application for a continuing detention order and extended supervision order against Mr Holt under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW).
cases.outcome: Adjournment granted; matter listed for further directions.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt (No 2)
cases.summary: Supreme Court application to adjourn and manage a Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act proceeding concerning interim detention of Mr Holt and related confidential terrorism-intelligence material.
cases.outcome: Hearing adjourned; matter fixed for further hearing and directions.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt (No 3)
cases.summary: The State sought a continuing detention order against Mr Holt and asked that a confidential exhibit be dealt with as terrorism intelligence. The Court held the exhibit was pre-existing document material lawfully obtained under s 58 and granted the terrorism intelligence application.
cases.outcome: Terrorism intelligence application granted; confidentiality maintained for the confidential exhibit.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt (No 4)
cases.summary: Adjournment in proceedings on the State of New South Wales’ application for an interim detention order against Mr Holt, involving confidential terrorism intelligence and suppression orders.
cases.outcome: Application for adjournment granted; the matter was adjourned for further argument.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt (No 5)
cases.summary: The Court refused leave for the plaintiff to orally examine an expert in chief about a terrorism risk assessment report, holding that exceptional circumstances were not shown.
cases.outcome: Leave refused.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt (No 6)
cases.summary: Proceeding in which the State sought a continuing detention order against Michael Holt and the Court addressed access to terrorism intelligence for that application.
cases.outcome: The Court amended earlier confidentiality orders so the relevant substance of the terrorism intelligence could be relayed to Holt.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt (No 8)
cases.summary: The State sought a continuing detention order, alternatively an extended supervision order, against Mr Holt under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). Campbell J held the risk was unacceptable unless Holt was supervised under an ESO and made a 3-year ESO with conditions.
cases.outcome: ESO made; CDO refused.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Holt (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court heard the State’s preliminary application under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW) for a continuing detention order or extended supervision order against Holt, and granted an interim detention order plus expert examinations.
cases.outcome: Orders granted at preliminary hearing.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Ibrahim (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted the State’s application for a 3-year extended supervision order and imposed conditions on Monzor Ibrahim after finding he had made statements advocating support for terrorist acts or violent extremism and posed an unacceptable risk if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: ESO made; application granted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Kiskonen (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The State sought an interim supervision order and related steps against Juha Kiskonen, alleging he had advocated support for violent extremism through UKOA material and threats toward police. The Court held the statutory threshold was not met and dismissed the amended summons.
cases.outcome: Application for interim/extended supervision orders refused.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Lawrence
cases.summary: Constitutional challenge to the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW) in proceedings brought by the State seeking supervision/detention relief against Tukiterangi Lawrence.
cases.outcome: The Court rejected the Kable/open justice challenge and held the Act constitutionally valid; the stay was lifted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Liddington (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW heard and determined the State’s application for an Extended Supervision Order against Desmond Liddington under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The Court found he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised and imposed a 12-month ESO with conditions.
cases.outcome: Extended Supervision Order granted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Liddington (No 1) (Media Application)
cases.summary: Media-access application in terrorism high-risk offender proceedings concerning Desmond Liddington. The Court refused access to most exhibits, allowed access to a criminal history summary, and made non-publication orders over parts of the evidence and submissions.
cases.outcome: Access to exhibits 1–7 denied; access to exhibit 8 allowed; non-publication orders made for specified evidence, submissions and transcript.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Mohommed Farhat (No 2) (Costs)
cases.summary: Costs decision arising from a preliminary hearing on the State’s application for an interim supervision order and expert examinations under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The interim supervision order was refused, experts were appointed, and the defendant was awarded half his costs of the preliminary hearing payable forthwith.
cases.outcome: Plaintiff ordered to pay 50% of the defendant’s costs of the preliminary hearing, payable forthwith.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Mustapha
cases.summary: The State sought expert-examination orders and an interim detention order (or alternatively an interim supervision order) against Mr Mustapha under the THRO Act. The Court found the statutory preconditions met, held he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if not detained, and made a 28-day interim detention order plus expert appointment orders.
cases.outcome: Application granted in part; interim detention ordered and experts appointed.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Mustapha (Final)
cases.summary: NSW Supreme Court granted Mr Mejid Mustapha an Extended Supervision Order for three years after finding, on consent, that he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Extended Supervision Order granted; interim detention order expired on commencement of the ESO.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Mustapha (Final)
acts_engaged: Post-sentence scheme — Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), a state equivalent, or Criminal Code Div 105A (Cth)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made a 1-year extended supervision order against Mejid Mustapha after finding he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order granted; conditions imposed.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Mustapha (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales considered whether the supporting material justified an extended supervision order for Mejid Mustapha and, at the preliminary stage, made examination orders and an interim supervision order for 28 days from expiry of the existing ESO. The Court accepted the statutory threshold was met, but omitted the proposed schedule-of-movements condition.
cases.outcome: Examination orders made; interim supervision order made; restricted-access order made; proposed schedule-of-movements condition deleted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Naaman
cases.summary: Court of Appeal stay application pending appeal about whether Mr Naaman should remain subject to an interim terrorism supervision order. The court granted the stay/suspension, reviving the interim supervision order until the appeal was heard.
cases.outcome: Stay/suspension granted pending appeal; interim supervision order revived for the stay period.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Naaman (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW dismissed the State’s application for an extended supervision order against Naaman and discharged the interim supervision order. The Court found he met the statutory threshold as a terrorism activity offender, but was not satisfied to a high degree of probability that he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed; interim supervision order discharged.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Naaman (No 2)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made an interim supervision order against Mohamed Naaman pending a final hearing under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017, finding the supporting material could justify an extended supervision order.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made for 28 days, with conditions to follow.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Osman
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of New South Wales made a three-year extended supervision order against Maywand Osman from 23 February 2021, imposing numerous restrictions on his movements, associations, communications, possessions and activities.
cases.outcome: Application granted; extended supervision order made.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v RC (Preliminary)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW granted an interim supervision order and related examination orders against RC under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), finding the supporting material could justify an extended supervision order because of his past extremist threats and related conduct.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order granted; defendant ordered to undergo psychiatric and psychological examinations; name suppressed.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Reginald Collingwood (A Pseudonym)
cases.summary: The State sought an interim supervision order and expert examination orders against Reginald Collingwood (a pseudonym) under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). Hamill J refused the application, holding the supporting material would not justify an extended supervision order.
cases.outcome: Application for an interim supervision order and s 24(5) expert orders dismissed; summons dismissed.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Taleb
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made an interim detention order for Mr Taleb under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW), with directions for psychiatric and psychological assessments, pending final determination of an application for a continuing detention order and extended supervision order.
cases.outcome: Application for interim relief granted; defendant placed on an interim detention order and ordered to undergo expert examinations.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Taleb (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW made a two-year Extended Supervision Order against Moudasser Taleb, with detailed conditions controlling movements, associations, devices, accommodation, substances, weapons, and extremist material, after finding he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence.
cases.outcome: ESO granted for two years from 16 December 2022, with amended supervision conditions.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v TL (Final)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court made a 3-year extended supervision order for TL under the THRO Act, after finding he posed an unacceptable risk of committing a serious terrorism offence if unsupervised.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order made for 3 years from 4 August 2022, with conditions imposed.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Wheatley (Preliminary)
cases.summary: Preliminary hearing under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court ordered psychiatric and psychological examinations, made an Interim Supervision Order, and imposed supervision conditions pending an Extended Supervision Order application.
cases.outcome: Application for interim relief granted.

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v White
cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW varied Mr White’s extended supervision order by reimposing electronic monitoring, subject to regular review and possible reimposition if he breached other conditions or his terrorism risk increased.
cases.outcome: Application granted; condition 4 of the supervision order was varied.

cases.summary: The State of NSW applied for and obtained an Interim Supervision Order against Greg Ceissman under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017. The application was based on alleged prison conversations in which he purportedly planned attacks on Marrickville Police Station and Bankstown targets, including explosives and shooting police.
cases.outcome: Interim Supervision Order granted; experts appointed; defendant ordered to attend examinations and comply with conditions.

cases.summary: Attorney General’s ex parte application for orders governing restricted service of Exhibit X 1, treated as terrorism intelligence, in proceedings against Ahmad Elomar. The Court granted the orders with a minor textual amendment.
cases.outcome: Application granted; Exhibit X 1 and related copies to be dealt with as terrorism intelligence and served/disclosed only under restricted conditions.

cases.summary: The State of NSW sought, and obtained, an extended supervision order for Ahmed Elomar for three years under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court considered his history of violence and terrorism-related risk material, accepted the proposed stringent conditions as necessary for community safety, and made consent orders.
cases.outcome: Extended supervision order made; consent orders approved.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court considered whether Mr Mathers should be subjected to an interim detention order or interim supervision order. The Court accepted that his threatening letters to a NSW MP advocated support for violent extremism, and imposed a 28-day interim supervision order with conditions and expert assessments.
cases.outcome: Interim supervision order made; interim detention order refused.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW imposed a two-year extended supervision order on John Mathers under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The Court found the statutory risk test was met and declined to refuse the order in discretion, while setting supervision conditions.
cases.outcome: ESO imposed for two years with conditions; pseudonym order and file-access restriction maintained.

cases.summary: The Supreme Court of NSW revoked an interim detention order previously made against TL under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 and instead imposed an interim supervision order for 28 days, with associated examination and compliance conditions.
cases.outcome: Interim detention order revoked; interim supervision order made.

cases.case_name: State of South Australia v Totani
cases.summary: High Court held s 14(1) of the Serious and Organised Crime (Control) Act 2008 (SA) invalid because it required the Magistrates Court to make control orders in a way incompatible with institutional integrity.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; s 14(1) invalid; special leave expanded to include later orders.

cases.summary: The Federal Court made an interim control order against Haisem Zahab after finding he had been convicted of providing support to Islamic State and that the proposed conditions were reasonably necessary and proportionate.
cases.outcome: Interim control order made; matter listed for confirmation hearing on 1 June 2026.

cases.summary: Federal Court proceedings on an application to confirm an interim control order made against the respondent, together with related suppression orders over parts of the court materials.
cases.outcome: Suppression orders were made over identified materials under s 37AF of the Federal Court of Australia Act.

cases.case_name: Talib v Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions
cases.summary: Bail application for a charge that the applicant assisted Witness One to prepare to enter Syria to engage in armed hostilities against the Syrian government. The court found exceptional-circumstances requirements applied and refused bail because the applicant was an unacceptable flight risk.
cases.outcome: Bail refused.

ideology_cause: support for hostile activity in Syria
cases.summary: The Federal Court confirmed an interim control order against Adam Mathew Brookman. The Court was satisfied he had been convicted in Australia of an offence relating to terrorism and that the imposed conditions were reasonably necessary and adapted to protect the public and prevent support for terrorist or hostile activity.
cases.outcome: Interim control order confirmed without variation and continued in force until 5 July 2024.
tags: support for hostile activity in Syria

cases.summary: High Court special case challenge to the constitutional validity of Div 104 of the Criminal Code (interim control orders) as applied to Joseph Thomas.
cases.outcome: Subdivision B of Div 104 was held valid; broader relief was refused. Thomas was ordered to pay the Commonwealth's costs.

acts_engaged: Criminal Code Act 1995 (Cth) Division 102 — proscription regime
cases.summary: The Federal Court dismissed an application for judicial review of the Minister for Home Affairs’ decision not to de-list Hamas under s 102.1(4) of the Criminal Code. The Court held the applicants had standing, but rejected arguments based on international law, procedural fairness, bias, RDA, and factual error.
cases.outcome: Originating application dismissed with costs.

cases.case_name: TYY v Office of Director of Public Prosecutions
cases.summary: Bail review for a child charged with an act in preparation for a deadly offence and possession of violent extremist material, arising from alleged plans to kill children and related extremist material possession.
cases.outcome: Application for review dismissed; bail refused.

ideology_cause: restoration of control of Indian occupied Kashmir to Muslims
cases.summary: Appeal from pre-trial rulings on an indictment charging Izhar Ul-Haque with intentionally receiving training from Lashkar-e-Taiba in Pakistan.
cases.outcome: Leave to raise grounds 1 and 2 granted but appeal dismissed; leave to raise ground 3 refused.
tags: restoration of control of Indian occupied Kashmir to Muslims

cases.case_name: Vinayagamoorthy v Director of Public Prosecutions (Cth)
acts_engaged: Charter of the United Nations Act 1945 (Cth)
cases.summary: Bail application for Aruran Vinayagamoorthy and Sivarajah Yathavan, who were charged with LTTE membership, financing and support offences; bail was granted on conditions.
cases.outcome: Bail granted to both accused pending committal.

cases.summary: High Court challenge to the constitutional validity of the NSW Crimes (Criminal Organisations Control) Act 2009, which allowed police to seek a declaration that the Hells Angels Motorcycle Club was a declared organisation and then obtain control orders against members.
cases.outcome: The majority held the Act invalid because Pt 2 undermined the institutional integrity of the Supreme Court of New South Wales; the plaintiff succeeded.

cases.case_name: White v Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP)
cases.summary: Appeal against sentence imposed in the Local Court for four breaches of an Extended Supervision Order, including use of prohibited online aliases and email names. The Supreme Court extended time, granted leave on one ground, and dismissed the appeal.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; time extended; leave granted to raise ground 4; sentence upheld.

cases.case_name: WWKJ and Minister for Foreign Affairs, Re
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: AAT review of ASIO’s adverse security assessment and the Minister for Foreign Affairs’ cancellation of WWKJ’s Australian passport on national security grounds tied to suspected politically motivated violence connected with ISIL support and intended travel overseas.
cases.outcome: The Tribunal affirmed both the adverse security assessment and the passport-cancellation decision.

cases.summary: The NSW Court of Criminal Appeal dismissed Zahab’s sentence appeal. He had pleaded guilty to intentionally providing support/resources to Islamic State by researching and developing a laser warning receiver, rockets and a rocket guidance method, and to failing to comply with a police order to provide passwords for encrypted devices.
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted; appeal dismissed.

cases.case_name: ZXYM and Director-General of Security, Re
ideology_cause: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)
acts_engaged: Australian Passports Act 2005 (Cth) and Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (Cth)
cases.summary: The Tribunal reviewed and affirmed an adverse ASIO security assessment concerning the applicant’s online sharing of ISIL propaganda and other extremist material, and his past support for ISIL, JFS and persons travelling to Syria.
cases.outcome: Decision affirmed; adverse security assessment upheld and visa cancellation recommendation maintained.
tags: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)

cases.summary: Forest protest in Tasmanian State forest, tree-sitting occupation to block logging access, March 1998
cases.main_issue: Whether sentencing took into account repeal of offence and whether fine was manifestly excessive
cases.outcome: Fine of $7,000 set aside; replaced with $5,000 fine recognising legislative changes and comparative sentencing

cases.court: Supreme Court of Western Australia - Court of Appeal
cases.summary: Protestors in Barrabup State Forest work site opposing logging, November 2001
cases.main_issue: Whether premises were sufficiently defined for conviction of unlawful remaining after police warning
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction upheld
cases.sanction_type: Conviction for remaining on premises without lawful authority

cases.court: Supreme Court of the Australian Capital Territory
acts_engaged: Public Order (Protection of Persons and Property) Act 1971 (Cth)
cases.summary: Aboriginal Australian protest involving fire at construction site near Lake Burley Griffin, Canberra, July 2001
cases.main_issue: Whether the appellant unlawfully refused to leave Commonwealth premises when directed, and procedural validity of prosecution consent
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and $500 fine upheld

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Street protest concerning refugee policy near the Immigration Minister's residence.
cases.main_issue: Whether to prohibit a notified public assembly under Part 4 of the Summary Offences Act 1988 (NSW).
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order refused.

cases.court: Supreme Court of the Northern Territory
cases.summary: protest at Northern Territory Legislative Assembly in Darwin, May 2002, disrupting parliamentary proceedings by entering chamber and displaying placards
cases.main_issue: whether the sentence imposed for intentionally disturbing the Legislative Assembly was manifestly excessive given appellant's minor role
cases.outcome: conviction confirmed; initial imprisonment sentence set aside and replaced with a good behaviour bond
cases.sanction_type: conviction confirmed; good behaviour bond imposed; imprisonment sentence quashed

cases.case_name: Minister for Industrial Development of Queensland v Taubenfeld
cases.case_type: Application for eviction and removal of protestors
cases.summary: Occupation protest at site of proposed food irradiation plant, Deception Bay 2002-2003
cases.main_issue: Appropriateness of appointing a representative defendant to represent fluid group of protestors for eviction orders
cases.outcome: Application dismissed for failure to establish representative defendant criteria
cases.sanction_type: No eviction or removal orders made; costs awarded

cases.case_type: Claim for damages for unlawful assault and wrongful arrest
acts_engaged: Vagrants, Gaming and Other Offences Act 1931 (Qld)
cases.summary: Plaintiff engaged in repeated protests advocating free speech in Townsville Mall, Queensland, including soliciting signatures and displaying flag and placards in late 1998 and 1999
cases.main_issue: Whether plaintiff's arrest by police officers for alleged by-law breaches and disorderly conduct was lawful and whether excessive force or wrongful imprisonment occurred
cases.outcome: Judgment for plaintiff against some defendants for compensatory damages due to unlawful arrest and assault; claim against others dismissed
cases.sanction_type: Damages awarded for unlawful assault and wrongful arrest; costs awarded

acts_engaged: Vagrants, Gaming and Other Offences Act 1931 (Qld)
cases.summary: Street political protest / pamphleteering against police corruption in Townsville.
cases.main_issue: Whether the insulting-words offence could validly burden political communication in the protest context.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed in substance; leading implied-freedom protest / street-speech authority.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Proposed protest near a police officer's home, framed as an anti-police corruption protest.
cases.main_issue: Whether the court should prohibit the assembly where the organiser's purpose was found to be largely vindictive.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order granted.

cases.case_name: McFadzean v Construction, Forestry, Mining & Energy Union
cases.summary: Environmental activists protesting against logging at Otway Ranges, Victoria, January 1999
cases.main_issue: Whether defendants falsely imprisoned plaintiffs (protesters) and committed other torts including assault, public nuisance, and Wilkinson v Downton claim
cases.outcome: Findings on false imprisonment, assault, and nuisance varied among plaintiffs and defendants with detailed analysis of tortious liability and damages

cases.court: Supreme Court of South Australia (Magistrates Appeals: Criminal)
cases.summary: Mass protest at Woomera Immigration Reception and Processing Centre, South Australia, 29 March 2002, involving a breach of detention facility and detainee escapes.
cases.main_issue: Whether the original sentence for escaping immigration detention was manifestly inadequate and whether the magistrate erred in considering deterrence and seriousness of the offence.
cases.outcome: Crown appeal allowed; original sentence set aside; offender re-sentenced to 3 months imprisonment released immediately on recognizance to be of good behaviour for 3 years.
cases.sanction_type: recognizance to be of good behaviour (good behaviour bond), custodial sentence imposed but released immediately

cases.court: Supreme Court of South Australia (Magistrates Appeals: Criminal)
cases.summary: Escape from Woomera Immigration Detention Centre during mass demonstration by approximately 250 protestors in 2002
cases.main_issue: Whether the sentencing magistrate erred by failing to consider the seriousness of the escape offence, the policy purpose of the Migration Act, and the need for general deterrence when sentencing
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; sentence of discharge without conviction on recognizance upheld
cases.sanction_type: Discharge without conviction upon recognizance bond

cases.summary: Mass demonstration protest at Woomera Immigration Reception and Processing Centre on 29 March 2002 encouraging detainees to escape
cases.main_issue: Whether the magistrate erred in sentencing process by failing to properly consider seriousness of offence and need for general deterrence when discharging defendant without conviction
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; sentence of discharge without conviction on good behaviour bond upheld despite error in sentencing process
cases.sanction_type: Discharge without conviction, good behaviour recognizance bond

acts_engaged: Tort — conspiracy and interference with trade
cases.summary: Timber company Gunns sued 20 environmental campaigners ('Gunns 20', incl. Bob Brown) for $6.3m over forest-protest campaigning.
cases.main_issue: Whether Gunns' statement of claim was adequately particularised.
cases.outcome: Statement of claim struck out; litigation widely seen as a SLAPP and later withdrawn.

cases.case_name: Police v Kakar; Elder v Kakar
cases.court: Supreme Court of South Australia (Magistrates Appeals: Criminal)
cases.summary: Large-scale protests at the Woomera Immigration Reception and Processing Centre, March and June 2002, involving detainees and external protestors facilitating detainee escapes
cases.main_issue: Whether the initial sentencing adequately reflected the seriousness of repeated immigration detention escapes and the need for deterrence, consistent with Migration Act policy
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; second escape offence convicted with recognizance for good behaviour (3 years) instead of dismissal without penalty
cases.sanction_type: Conviction with release upon recognizance to be of good behaviour, no immediate custody

cases.case_name: S v Secretary, Department of Immigration & Multicultural & Indigenous Affairs
ideology_cause: Immigration detention / detainee rights / mental health care
cases.summary: Immigration detainees mental health treatment dispute arising from prolonged detention and related hunger strike protest at Baxter Detention Centre, South Australia, 2004-2005
cases.main_issue: Whether Commonwealth breached duty of care to immigration detainees by failing to provide adequate mental health care and timely psychiatric assessment, including after hunger strike protest
cases.outcome: Applications dismissed as detainees had been transferred for assessment; applicants entitled to costs
cases.sanction_type: Dismissal of application; costs awarded to applicants
tags: Immigration detention / detainee rights / mental health care

cases.case_name: Corrigan v City of Sydney Council and anor
cases.court: Administrative Decisions Tribunal of New South Wales, Equal Opportunities Division
cases.case_type: Application for leave to proceed (anti-discrimination complaint)
cases.summary: Application to stage a re-enactment of the 1916 Easter uprising at Sydney Square in 2004
cases.main_issue: Whether refusal by Glebe Administration Board and City of Sydney Council to grant permission was unlawful racial discrimination
cases.outcome: Application for leave to proceed refused for lack of evidence linking refusal to race

cases.court: Court of Appeal of the Northern Territory
cases.summary: Anti-prohibition protest in Northern Territory Legislative Assembly chamber in 2002
cases.main_issue: Whether appellants disturbed Legislative Assembly in session and related constitutional and privilege challenges
cases.outcome: Appeals against conviction dismissed with costs

cases.case_name: White & Ors v State of South Australia & Ors
cases.case_type: Miscellaneous appeal (discovery and inspection of documents)
cases.summary: Peaceful protest at Beverley uranium mine, Arkaroola, May 2000
cases.main_issue: Whether defendants must produce police complaints investigation documents despite secrecy provisions under the Police (Complaints and Disciplinary Proceedings) Act 1985
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; defendants ordered to produce investigation documents subject to privilege

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Protesters at logging operations in Yambulla State Forest, NSW, 2004
cases.main_issue: Whether failure to comply with authorised officer's request under Forestry Regulation 1999 clause 15(3) constituted offence, specifically if officer properly informed individual about offence
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed, order of dismissal set aside, case remitted to Local Court for determination according to law
cases.sanction_type: Appeal decision, remittal to Local Court

cases.case_name: New South Wales Commissioner of Police v Bainbridge
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
ideology_cause: Anti-war/Iraq War, Climate change, Workersâ€™ rights
cases.summary: Stop Bush Coalition's planned protest in Sydney on 8 September 2007 against Australian Government policies on Iraq and Afghanistan wars, climate change, and workers' rights during APEC visit by US President Bush
cases.main_issue: Whether to prohibit the proposed public assembly due to public safety and security risks arising from large crowds, confined venues and potential for violence
cases.outcome: Court prohibited the proposed public assembly route, requiring a safer alternative route, effectively restricting the assembly as proposed
tags: Anti-war/Iraq War, Climate change, Workersâ€™ rights

cases.case_name: Padraic Gibson & Ors v Commissioner of Police & Ors
cases.summary: APEC protest march in Sydney against Iraq/Afghanistan, nuclear issues, and WorkChoices
cases.main_issue: Whether APEC security powers burdened and invalidly infringed the implied freedom of political communication
cases.outcome: Summons dismissed with costs; restrictions upheld

cases.case_name: R v Law & Ors (Pine Gap Four)
cases.court: Supreme Court of the Northern Territory
cases.summary: Trial of the Pine Gap Four; defendants sought to put emergency/self-defence/international-law defences to the jury over their Iraq-war protest incursion.
cases.main_issue: Whether necessity/self-defence/lawful-authority defences were available for political civil disobedience.
cases.outcome: Defences not left to the jury; jury convicted.

cases.case_name: R v Law & Ors (Pine Gap Four)
cases.court: Supreme Court of the Northern Territory
cases.summary: Pre-trial in the Pine Gap Four prosecution; self-represented defendants sought discovery of the Minister's prohibited-area declaration material.
cases.main_issue: Whether the defendants were entitled to discovery of the Ministerial decision-making material.
cases.outcome: Discovery application refused (later held flawed on appeal).

cases.case_name: White & Ors v State of South Australia & Ors
cases.court: Supreme Court of South Australia (Full Court)
cases.summary: Protests at Beverley uranium mine near Arkaroola, May 2000
cases.main_issue: Whether police documents related to investigation of protest conduct should be disclosed despite statutory secrecy provisions
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; order requiring disclosure of documents set aside; immunity from production upheld

cases.case_name: Paramasivam v State of New South Wales (No.3)
cases.case_type: Discrimination application under Racial Discrimination Act
ideology_cause: Free speech / protest rights - trespass and protest at University
cases.summary: Applicant protested by refusing to leave UNSW premises during 2003-2004 by attending Vice-Chancellor's office; arrested for trespass on four occasions.
cases.main_issue: Whether police conduct during arrests involved unlawful racial discrimination under Racial Discrimination Act 1975 (Cth).
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; no evidence of racial discrimination by police found.
tags: Free speech / protest rights - trespass and protest at University

cases.case_name: R v Law & Ors (Pine Gap Four)
cases.court: Supreme Court of the Northern Territory - Court of Criminal Appeal
cases.summary: Four 'Christians Against All Terrorism' activists entered the Pine Gap defence facility (Dec 2005) to protest Australia's role in the Iraq war.
cases.main_issue: Whether the prohibited-area declaration was wrongly treated as conclusive, withdrawing an element from the jury.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; Defence (Special Undertakings) Act convictions quashed; acquittals entered.

cases.court: Supreme Court of Victoria, Court of Appeal
provisions_engaged: including s 320 (riot), aggravated burglary and criminal damage provisions
cases.summary: Violent protest and riots during 2006 G20 Economic Summit in Melbourne, involving entry to Defence Force Recruiting Office and attacks on police and staff in CBD

cases.main_issue: Whether safe-access-zone restrictions around abortion clinics impermissibly burdened political communication.
cases.outcome: Victorian safe-access-zone law upheld.

cases.case_name: Commissioner of Police v Da Costa-Reidel
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Newtown rally / march on a heavily trafficked route.
cases.main_issue: Whether route choice, ambulance access and traffic disruption justified prohibition.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order granted.

cases.summary: Anti-mosque protest in Bendigo, Victoria, October 2015 involving a mock Islamic-style beheading video

cases.case_name: Grajewski v Director of Public Prosecutions (NSW)

cases.case_name: Shortis v Chief Commissioner of Police
cases.summary: 2015 mock beheading protest against mosque development in Bendigo, Victoria
cases.main_issue: Whether applicant was fit and proper person and if granting licence was in the public interest given conviction under Racial and Religious Tolerance Act
cases.outcome: Licence refusal affirmed

cases.case_name: Adani Mining Pty Ltd v Pennings
acts_engaged: Tort — conspiracy and interference with trade
cases.summary: Adani/Carmichael Rail sued Galilee Blockade anti-coal activist Ben Pennings alleging intimidation and misuse of confidential info.
cases.main_issue: Whether an Anton Piller search order should be granted against the activist.
cases.outcome: Search order refused.

cases.case_name: Adani Mining Pty Ltd v Pennings
cases.court: Supreme Court of Queensland - Court of Appeal
cases.summary: Appeal in the Galilee Blockade dispute concerning anti-coal activist Ben Pennings.
cases.main_issue: Whether refusal of the Anton Piller order should be overturned.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; search order refused.

cases.case_name: Attorney-General for the State of Queensland v Sri & Ors
cases.summary: Planned Story Bridge sit-in protest during COVID-19.
cases.main_issue: Whether the State should obtain injunctive relief to stop the protest.
cases.outcome: Injunction granted in favour of the State.

cases.court: Court of Appeal of New South Wales
acts_engaged: Constitution (Cth) — implied freedom of political communication
cases.summary: Appeal arising from the Sydney Black Lives Matter vigil decision.
cases.main_issue: Whether procedural / notice issues required reversal of the first-instance outcome.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed on narrow notice/procedural grounds; the Court of Appeal did not re-do the underlying discretionary balancing exercise.

cases.summary: Anti-abortion activist Kathleen Clubb appealed her conviction for communicating about abortion within a safe-access zone (post-HCA remitter).
cases.main_issue: Whether there was evidence of a prohibited 'communication in relation to abortion' under s 185D.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction upheld.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Sydney CBD Black Lives Matter / David Dungay Jr justice protest during COVID-19.
cases.main_issue: Whether a large city protest should be prohibited because of health and public order concerns.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order granted.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Refugee-rights protest about infection risk for people in detention during COVID-19.
cases.main_issue: Whether COVID-era health risks justified prohibition.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order granted.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Black Lives Matter vigil in Sydney during COVID-19 restrictions.
cases.main_issue: Whether the court should authorise the assembly or prohibit it given public health risks.
cases.outcome: Authorisation refused at first instance; police position prevailed.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Newcastle Black Lives Matter / anti-racism / deaths-in-custody protest during COVID-19.
cases.main_issue: Whether the protest could proceed despite pandemic restrictions and public health concerns.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order refused.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Community Action for Rainbow Rights protest concerning transgender schoolchildren / gender and sexuality advice issues during COVID-19.
cases.main_issue: Whether the protest should be prohibited, including in light of alternative means of advocacy and public health concerns.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order granted.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Wollongong assembly / procession during COVID-19.
cases.main_issue: Whether the proposed protest should be prohibited because pandemic risks outweighed the planned assembly.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order granted.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: National Tertiary Education Union NSW protest in Camperdown / Victoria Park during COVID-19, with a detailed safety plan.
cases.main_issue: Whether to prohibit the proposed assembly despite a detailed COVID safety plan.
cases.outcome: Police summons dismissed; prohibition refused.

cases.summary: Climate-protest prosecutions involving dangerous attachment / railway obstruction style offences.

cases.summary: Activist group sued VicForests over logging of 66 Central Highlands coupes affecting threatened species.
cases.main_issue: Whether VicForests' logging complied with the Code such that the RFA/EPBC exemption applied.
cases.outcome: Friends largely succeeded; breaches found.

cases.court: Court of Appeal of New South Wales
cases.summary: Appeal arising from the Sydney CBD Black Lives Matter protest case.
cases.main_issue: Whether appellate relief was available given the statutory scheme and technical / jurisdictional issues.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed / first-instance prohibition stood.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Animal rights activists entered a property in Lakesland, NSW in June 2018 to rescue battery hens from alleged cruelty
cases.main_issue: Whether the defence of necessity applied to plaintiffs' aggravated unlawful entry and interference with business
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted but appeal dismissed; convictions and fines upheld
cases.sanction_type: Fine of $1500 imposed on each plaintiff

cases.summary: Anti-Adani/anti-coal activist attached himself to a tripod over the rail line at Bowen, blocking the Adani/Aurizon coal railway.
cases.main_issue: Whether a climate-emergency necessity defence applied and whether the fines were excessive.
cases.outcome: Conviction stood; necessity rejected; fines reduced from $7,000 to $3,000.

cases.case_name: The Association of Professional Engineers, Scientists and Managers, Australia

cases.summary: Protest in support of refugees seeking asylum in Australia, NSW, 2017
cases.main_issue: Whether the applicant is a fit and proper person to hold a right of entry permit under the Fair Work Act 2009
cases.outcome: Permit issued to the applicant after consideration of prior conviction and other qualifications

cases.court: Supreme Court of Queensland - Court of Appeal
cases.case_type: Miscellaneous Application - Civil - Removal of parties and appeal jurisdiction challenge
cases.summary: Appeal against prohibition of public assembly notice under Peaceful Assembly Act 1992 (Qld) involving proposed protest assembly by Arjay Rase Martin
cases.main_issue: Whether District Court had jurisdiction to hear an appeal under Peaceful Assembly Act 1992 (Qld) and whether certain parties should be removed from proceedings
cases.outcome: Court held District Court lacked jurisdiction to hear appeal and ordered removal of applicants from proceedings; costs awarded to applicants
cases.sanction_type: Prohibition of public assembly upheld; removal of parties from appeal; costs order against appellant

cases.case_name: Adani Mining Pty Ltd & anor v Pennings
cases.case_type: Application for confidentiality regime and disclosure limitations in civil proceedings
cases.summary: Environmental activists (Galilee Blockade) opposing Carmichael Mine and Rail, Queensland, since 2017
cases.main_issue: Whether a confidentiality regime should be imposed on disclosure of confidential information allegedly misused by protest campaigner to disrupt Adani operations
cases.outcome: Court imposed partial confidentiality orders limiting defendant's access to confidential documents with redactions and regulated inspection conditions
cases.sanction_type: Confidentiality regime with redactions and restricted access orders

cases.case_name: Antaw v R; Kitson v R; Lee v R
cases.court: District Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Protesters directed to move on during a road-blocking protest were convicted of failing to comply with a police direction.
cases.main_issue: Whether a LEPRA s 197 move-on direction requires actual obstruction or only reasonable belief.
cases.outcome: Appeals dismissed; s 197 requires only reasonable belief; convictions upheld.

cases.case_name: Australian Building and Construction Commissioner v Holl (The Wheeler Cranes Case)
ideology_cause: Industrial relations/protest related to union enterprise bargaining negotiations
acts_engaged: Building and Construction Industry (Improving Productivity) Act 2016 (Cth)
cases.summary: Protest at multiple Newcastle construction sites, October 2018, disrupting crane operations by Wheeler Cranes during union enterprise bargaining dispute
cases.main_issue: Whether respondents contravened s 355(b) and s 500 of Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) and s 52(b) of Building and Construction Industry (Improving Productivity) Act 2016 (Cth) via coercive and obstructive conduct

cases.case_name: Australian Conservation Foundation Inc v Minister for the Environment
acts_engaged: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (Cth)
cases.summary: ACF (Stop Adani) challenged a decision that the North Galilee Water Scheme for the Carmichael mine did not need EPBC water-trigger assessment.
cases.main_issue: Whether the water infrastructure required assessment under the EPBC water trigger.
cases.outcome: Application granted; decision to be reconsidered.

cases.case_name: Bob Brown Foundation Inc v Commonwealth of Australia
cases.court: Full Court of the Federal Court of Australia
acts_engaged: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (Cth)
cases.summary: BBF (Tasmanian anti-logging campaign) sought to establish that the Tasmanian RFA did not exempt native-forest logging from the EPBC Act.
cases.main_issue: Whether the Tasmanian RFA was a valid RFA attracting the EPBC forestry exemption.
cases.outcome: Separate question answered against BBF; relief refused.

cases.summary: Kelly Cotterill left home during Melbourne's COVID lockdown with an anti-Premier protest sign, challenging the Stay at Home Directions.
cases.main_issue: Whether the lockdown directions impermissibly burdened the implied freedom.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; restrictions did not impermissibly burden the freedom.

cases.summary: Request for documents on police resources allocated to anti-lockdown protests in Melbourne
cases.main_issue: Whether documents relating to police resources at anti-lockdown protests are exempt from disclosure under FOI Act section 31(1)(d)
cases.outcome: FOI request refusal not upheld; agency required to search for and assess relevant documents, possibly providing edited copies
cases.sanction_type: Order to search for and assess documents, with obligation to disclose non-exempt parts

cases.case_name: Kassam v Hazzard; Henry v Hazzard
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Anti-mandate 'freedom' movement challenge to NSW COVID-19 public health orders requiring vaccination.
cases.main_issue: Whether the public health orders were unreasonable or beyond power.
cases.outcome: Challenges dismissed; orders upheld.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Paramedic associated with anti-mandate advocacy challenged COVID-19 vaccination public health orders.
cases.main_issue: Whether the orders were legally unreasonable/disproportionate.
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; later CA appeal also dismissed.

cases.case_name: Re application for bail by Smit
cases.summary: Anti-lockdown protests in Melbourne during COVID-19 pandemic, 2020-2021
cases.main_issue: Whether bail conditions imposed on protest leader Monica Smit were reasonable and proportionate to prevent reoffending and endangering public welfare
cases.outcome: Bail granted with varied conduct conditions limiting incitement and requiring residence at specified address
cases.sanction_type: Conduct conditions on bail, including prohibitions on incitement and non-compliance with health directions

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales - Court of Appeal
cases.summary: Animal-rights activist entered a poultry farm with others to 'rescue' caged chickens she alleged were mistreated.
cases.main_issue: Whether the necessity defence is available where the harm avoided is to animals, not a person.
cases.outcome: Leave refused; conviction upheld - necessity requires apprehended harm to a person.

cases.case_name: VicForests v Friends of Leadbeater's Possum Inc
cases.court: Full Court of the Federal Court of Australia
acts_engaged: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (Cth)
cases.summary: VicForests' appeal against the finding that its logging breached environmental law.
cases.main_issue: Whether RFA forestry operations were exempt from the EPBC Act despite state-law breaches.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; logging held exempt under the RFA.

cases.case_name: Australian Building and Construction Commissioner v Construction, Forestry, Maritime, Mining and Energy Union (The 250 East Terrace Case)
cases.court: Federal Court of Australia, Fair Work Division
ideology_cause: Industrial dispute over payment in building and construction sector
acts_engaged: Building and Construction Industry (Improving Productivity) Act 2016 (Cth)

cases.case_name: Bob Brown Foundation Inc v Minister for the Environment (No 2)
