cases.main_issue: Whether the delegate failed to consider the precautionary principle (Tasmanian Masked Owl).
cases.outcome: Application succeeded; decision affected by error.

cases.case_name: Bob Brown Foundation Inc v Sustainable Timber Tasmania
cases.court: Supreme Court of Tasmania - Full Court
cases.summary: BBF (takayna/Tarkine anti-logging) sought access to timber-production land to hold an anti-logging fundraising event; access refused; proceedings discontinued.
cases.main_issue: Whether the primary judge erred in declining costs (incl. model-litigant arguments).
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; 'no order as to costs' stood.

cases.case_name: Buckley v Council of the Law Society of New South Wales
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Solicitor's suspension following public and social media comments during COVID-19 related litigation and protests
cases.main_issue: Whether the Council committed jurisdictional error by suspending plaintiff's practising certificate without properly considering implied freedom of political communication and alternative sanctions
cases.outcome: Application dismissed; no jurisdictional error found; suspension upheld

cases.case_name: Conservation Council of WA (Inc) v Hatton
cases.summary: Conservation Council challenged the EPA chair's approval of changes to the Woodside Pluto LNG project.
cases.main_issue: Whether the approval of project changes was lawful.
cases.outcome: Applications dismissed; EPA approval upheld.

cases.summary: Appellant disrupted a religious service by the Metropolitan Community Church of Melbourne in Hawthorn in May 2019
cases.main_issue: Whether the appellant wilfully disturbed a meeting of persons lawfully assembled for religious worship contrary to s 21 of the Summary Offences Act 1966 (Vic)

cases.case_name: Farm Transparency International Ltd v New South Wales
acts_engaged: Constitution (Cth) — implied freedom of political communication
cases.summary: Animal-rights group challenged NSW surveillance laws used against activists who covertly filmed alleged animal cruelty on farms.
cases.main_issue: Whether ss 11-12 Surveillance Devices Act burden the implied freedom of political communication.
cases.outcome: Challenge largely failed; provisions upheld (majority).

cases.case_name: In the matter of the Entry Permit of Justin Brendon Lee Hobson
ideology_cause: Labor union-related industrial protest and workplace rights enforcement
acts_engaged: Building and Construction Industry (Improving Productivity) Act 2016 (Cth)

cases.main_issue: Whether to suspend or revoke union organiser's entry permit following contraventions of s 500 of Fair Work Act 2009 relating to obstruction and hindrance during exercise of entry rights
cases.outcome: Suspension of Mr Hobson's entry permit for 3 months with a 3-month ban on re-issue
cases.sanction_type: Suspension of entry permit and temporary ban on re-issue

cases.case_name: Media, Entertainment and Arts Alliance v Fair Work Commission
cases.summary: Union organiser applying for entry permit after previous protest charge related to anti-offshore detention protest in Sydney
cases.main_issue: Whether the applicant is a fit and proper person to hold a right of entry permit under the Fair Work Act 2009
cases.outcome: Entry permit granted to applicant; no conditions imposed

cases.summary: peaceful protest at QV1 office tower Perth, October 2020
cases.main_issue: whether behaviour of costumed performer pressing posterior against window was offensive disorderly conduct under s 74A Criminal Code (WA)
cases.outcome: appeal allowed; conviction set aside; acquittal substituted

cases.case_type: Judicial review of magistrate's data access order

cases.outcome: Application for judicial review dismissed; magistrate's order upheld
cases.sanction_type: Judicial review dismissal; order requiring compliance with s 465AA access order

cases.case_name: Van Niekerk v State of Victoria (Victoria Police)

cases.main_issue: Whether police conduct towards applicant during protests constituted discrimination in provision of goods or services under Equal Opportunity Act

cases.case_name: Brisbane City Council v Le Roy

cases.case_type: Appeal from Tribunal decision on representative complaint status

cases.main_issue: Whether complaint by Ms Le Roy regarding BCC's ban on XR bookings should be treated as a representative complaint under the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 (Qld)
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal refused; complaint to proceed as a representative complaint for Queensland XR members
cases.sanction_type: No sanction; procedural ruling allowing representative complaint status

cases.case_name: Commissioner of Police v Rising Tide (Newcastle coal port)
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Rising Tide's 'People's Blockade of the World's Largest Coal Port' in Newcastle.
cases.main_issue: Whether to prohibit the notified public assembly.

Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 2009 (SA)
cases.summary: Protest at 250 East Terrace construction site, Adelaide, October 2019, over unpaid subcontractor claims
cases.main_issue: Whether pecuniary penalties for unlawful picketing were appropriate and proportionate
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; penalties upheld

cases.court: Supreme Court of Victoria - Court of Appeal
cases.summary: Appeal from the anti-lockdown protest challenge to Melbourne COVID movement restrictions.
cases.main_issue: Whether the emergency directions impermissibly burdened the implied freedom.
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; directions valid.

cases.case_name: Cullen v State of New South Wales

cases.main_issue: Whether police owed and breached a duty of care to rally attendees and caused injury to a spectator
cases.outcome: Plaintiff succeeded at first instance; judgment for $800,000

cases.court: Supreme Court of the Australian Capital Territory
cases.summary: Protest at Old Parliament House in ACT, December 2021 concerning Aboriginal sovereignty and justice
cases.main_issue: Appropriate sentence for arson and obstruction during politically motivated protest causing significant property damage

cases.case_name: Edwards v Police; Weber v Police; Homewood v Police
cases.summary: Climate change protest by Extinction Rebellion on 18 May 2023 at Santos Ltd building, Adelaide.
cases.main_issue: Whether the sentences imposed for property damage offences during protest were justified and if the magistrate provided adequate reasons.

cases.case_name: Glover v R; Coco v R

cases.summary: Fireproof Australia climate activists ('Violet' Coco and Alan Glover) blocked a lane of the Sydney Harbour Bridge with a truck and lit a flare (April 2022).

cases.case_name: Kvelde v State of New South Wales

cases.summary: Challenge to NSW 'major facility' anti-protest offences used against blockade / disruption protests.
cases.main_issue: Whether s 214A and related anti-protest provisions impermissibly burdened the implied freedom of political communication.

cases.case_name: Lawton v State of Victoria (Victoria Police)

cases.case_name: Mo v Director of Public Prosecutions

cases.summary: Applicant protested at pro-Hong Kong democracy rally at University of Queensland, July 2019
cases.main_issue: Whether consular immunity applied to respondent's alleged threatening statement relating to protest violence and whether extension of time to appeal should be granted

cases.case_name: Stratton v State of New South Wales; Pandolfi v Minister for Health and Medical Research

cases.case_name: Tey v State of New South Wales; Altakrity v State of New South Wales
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales

cases.case_name: Application by Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union for Shane Reside

cases.case_name: Application by the Chief Commissioner of Victoria Police under section 21B of the Terrorism (Community Protection) Act 2003

cases.summary: Bob Brown (79) arrested in the Styx Valley (Feb 2024) during anti-logging protest.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Rising Tide Newcastle coal-port protest / march.

cases.case_name: Hunter Community Environment Centre Inc v Browne
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Blockade Australia-related protest activities in Newcastle, November 2021; search warrants executed at community and residential premises linked to protestors
cases.main_issue: Validity of police-issued search warrants related to protest activity and whether police had reasonable grounds and properly issued warrants
cases.outcome: Application to file summons out of time granted; judicial review summons dismissed; plaintiffs ordered to pay defendants' costs

cases.case_name: Kvelde v State of New South Wales (No 2)
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Follow-on judgment to the Knitting Nannas challenge ([2023] NSWSC 1560) to NSW anti-protest amendments.
cases.main_issue: Consequential orders and costs after partial striking-down of Crimes Act s 214A.
cases.outcome: Consequential declarations/orders following the plaintiffs' partial success.

cases.case_type: Appeal pursuant to s 222 of the Justices Act 1886 (Qld)
ideology_cause: Political expression concerning Tiananmen Square, pro-democracy commentary
acts_engaged: Public Land and Council Assets Local Law 2014 (Brisbane City Council)
cases.summary: Displaying placards about Tiananmen Square massacre and political messages in Queen Street Mall, Brisbane, May 2022
cases.main_issue: Whether displaying a placard without consent constituted an offence under Local Law and whether restrictions infringed freedom of expression rights
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; convictions and fines upheld
cases.sanction_type: Fine ($1,000 per charge), court costs, no conviction recorded
tags: Political expression concerning Tiananmen Square, pro-democracy commentary

cases.summary: Prosecutions following SA's 2023 obstruction-of-public-places amendments (triggered by an Extinction Rebellion APPEA-conference protest).
cases.main_issue: Penalties under the new $50,000 maximum obstruction regime.
cases.outcome: Various fines imposed under the amended regime.

cases.case_name: R v Brown (Eastern Tiers forestry trespass)
cases.citation: Magistrates Court of Tasmania, Comments on Passing Sentence, 14 Aug 2024
cases.summary: Bob Brown Foundation founder Bob Brown found in a logging coupe during Sustainable Timber Tasmania operations (Nov 2022) and refused to leave.
cases.main_issue: Whether trespass was proven and whether to record a conviction.
cases.outcome: Found guilty; fined $500, no conviction recorded; appeal foreshadowed.

cases.court: County Court of Victoria, Common Law Division
cases.case_type: civil claim for tort of false imprisonment
cases.summary: Anti-lockdown protest at Treasury Gardens, Melbourne on 31 October 2020
cases.main_issue: Lawfulness of three arrests of protestor under s458 of Crimes Act 1958 for breach of CHO directions during COVID-19 lockdown
cases.outcome: Court found two of the three arrests were unlawful (false imprisonment); damages awarded to plaintiff

cases.case_name: State of New South Wales v Cullen
cases.summary: Invasion Day protest march; police entered crowd during operational response
cases.main_issue: Whether police owed/breached a duty of care and whether police action caused injury to rally spectator
cases.outcome: Appeal upheld; trial judgment set aside; claim dismissed

cases.case_name: The Game Meats Company of Australia Pty Ltd v Farm Transparency International Ltd
cases.summary: Animal-rights activists covertly entered a Victorian goat abattoir seven times to film alleged cruelty; the operator sued for trespass and to restrain publication.
cases.main_issue: Whether to restrain publication of covertly-obtained footage and award trespass damages.
cases.outcome: Relief granted restraining publication; damages awarded against the activists.

cases.court: Queensland Body Corporate and Community Management Commissioner - Adjudicators Orders
ideology_cause: Free speech / protest within body corporate community
acts_engaged: Body Corporate and Community Management Act 1997 (Qld)
cases.summary: Owner's ongoing protest communication, banners, and megaphone announcements at Tristan Place residential community (Benowa, Qld) since 2022
cases.main_issue: Whether respondent's protest conduct and communication contravened body corporate by-laws relating to nuisance and unreasonable interference
cases.outcome: Orders restricting respondent's communication to be reasonable and not cause nuisance; removal of protest signs and banners within seven days; other orders declined
tags: Free speech / protest within body corporate community

cases.summary: Protest at Labour Day function in Brisbane in May 2024 supporting Palestine and opposing Queensland Premier
cases.main_issue: Whether spitting on police officer's boot constitutes assault by applying force to the person of the officer
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed, conviction upheld

cases.case_name: Application by Chief Commissioner of Police (Pillars of Light)
cases.summary: Application for special police powers around a public event under counter-terrorism legislation.
cases.main_issue: Whether to authorise special police powers under Pt 3A.
cases.outcome: Orders granted; special police powers authorised.

cases.case_type: judicial review (motion to review magistrate's decision)
cases.summary: Environmental protest at forestry coupe SH045A, Tasmania, November 2022, concerning logging and swift parrot habitat protection
cases.main_issue: Whether the applicant trespassed by remaining on permanent timber production zone land after a lawful request to leave was made, and if lawful or reasonable excuses (including freedom of conscience) applied
cases.outcome: Conviction for trespass upheld; fine imposed without a recorded conviction
cases.sanction_type: Fine ($500) without conviction recorded, and court costs

cases.court: Supreme Court of Victoria (Common Law Division)
cases.case_type: civil claim - police torts claim for battery and assault
cases.summary: protest outside Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre against IMARC conference, October 2019
cases.main_issue: whether use of OC foam by police was lawful and proportionate use of force under Crimes Act and common law during arrests of pole climbers and surrounding protestors
cases.outcome: court allowed some amendments to state defence clarifying use of force reasons but refused late amendments relating to an additional arrest; case ongoing

cases.case_name: Brown v State of Victoria (No 3) (IMARC class action)
cases.summary: Class action against Victoria Police over use of OC (capsicum) foam against anti-mining (IMARC conference) protesters in Melbourne.
cases.main_issue: Whether police use of OC foam constituted battery.
cases.outcome: Court found OC foam deployments constituted battery of the lead plaintiff.

cases.summary: Retired anaesthetist Dr Lee Ann Coaldrake (71) and 13 other Extinction Rebellion members disrupted Qld Parliament.
cases.main_issue: Whether 'disturbing the Legislature' offence made out.
cases.outcome: Convicted; fined $5,000.

cases.case_name: Commissioner of Police (NSW Police Force) v Joshua Lees
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Planned Gaza-related protest on the Sydney Harbour Bridge.
cases.main_issue: Whether a highly disruptive symbolic bridge protest should be prohibited.
cases.outcome: Police prohibition order refused.

cases.case_name: Commissioner of Police (NSW Police Force) v Naser
cases.summary: Palestine Action Group procession to Sydney Opera House forecourt concerning Gaza
cases.main_issue: Whether the proposed public assembly should be prohibited under s 25 of the Summary Offences Act and whether constitutional/free communication issues affected that result
cases.outcome: Public assembly prohibited; cross-summons dismissed

cases.case_name: Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union - The Maritime Union of Australia Division - Sydney Branch
cases.case_type: Application for right of entry permit
ideology_cause: Industrial rights and workplace dispute actions, including participation in a political protest regarding Gaza
cases.summary: MUA officials involvement in industrial actions related to workplace disputes in Sydney, including a peaceful Gaza protest in 2024
cases.main_issue: Whether the applicant official, Mr Paul Keating, is a fit and proper person to hold a right of entry permit under the Fair Work Act 2009
cases.outcome: The application for a right of entry permit was granted, with no conditions imposed, accepting the applicant is now fit and proper after training and reflection despite past contraventions
cases.sanction_type: Permit issued, previously involved in penalties/fines and good behaviour bond, no new sanctions imposed
tags: Industrial rights and workplace dispute actions, including participation in a political protest regarding Gaza

cases.case_name: Cullen v State of New South Wales
cases.summary: Invasion Day rally; police crowd-control response and injury to spectator
cases.main_issue: Whether police operational decisions created foreseeable risk and legal liability for injury during protest policing
cases.outcome: Transcript of High Court argument; no final orders in transcript

cases.court: Supreme Court of the Australian Capital Territory
cases.summary: Large political protest outside Parliament House, Canberra, February 2022, concerning COVID-19 mandates
cases.main_issue: Whether driving a vehicle at or near police officers at a protest constituted reckless endangerment and warranted conviction and sentencing
cases.outcome: Convicted on two counts of driving at or near police, fined $1,000 on each count with 6 months to pay

cases.summary: Protest relating to alleged contravention of Chief Health Officer directions during public assembly in East Melbourne, 2021
cases.main_issue: Whether judicial review proceedings on convictions for failure to comply with health directions were commenced in time and whether there are special circumstances to extend time
cases.outcome: Applications for extension of time to commence judicial review proceedings dismissed with costs; proceedings dismissed
cases.sanction_type: fine without conviction, extension of time refused, dismissal of proceedings

cases.case_name: Le Roy v Brisbane City Council
cases.summary: Extinction Rebellion organising and use of council meeting rooms
cases.main_issue: Whether banning Extinction Rebellion from booking council facilities was discrimination based on political belief or activity
cases.outcome: Complaint upheld; council ordered to stop enforcing the ban and notify class members

cases.case_name: Lees v State of New South Wales
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
acts_engaged: Constitution (Cth) — implied freedom of political communication
cases.summary: Challenge to NSW restriction on protest near places of worship.
cases.main_issue: Whether s 200(5) LEPRA impermissibly burdened the implied freedom of political communication.
cases.outcome: Restriction held invalid.

cases.case_name: Pabai Pabai v Commonwealth of Australia
cases.summary: Torres Strait Islander elders sought recognition of a duty of care re climate change harm to their islands.
cases.main_issue: Whether the Commonwealth owes a duty of care to protect Torres Strait Islanders from climate impacts.
cases.outcome: Claim dismissed; no duty of care. Appeal filed Nov 2025.

cases.court: District Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Group of men including appellant dressed in black and face coverings, on train and railway premises on Australia Day 2024, linked to far-right display
cases.main_issue: Whether appellant wilfully interfered with the comfort of other persons under Passenger Transport (General) Regulation 2017
cases.outcome: Conviction and penalty confirmed, appeal dismissed

acts_engaged: Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act 2006 (Vic)
cases.summary: Use of insulting words in a public place during political communication context in Melbourne
cases.main_issue: Definition and interpretation of 'insulting words' under s 17(1)(c) Summary Offences Act 1966 (Vic) and its compatibility with freedom of expression under the Charter and implied freedom of political communication
cases.outcome: Court applied a wide approach to 'insulting words' incorporating context of political communication and general intent to use words as insulting; provision held compatible with Charter and implied freedom

cases.court: Supreme Court of Victoria, Criminal Division
ideology_cause: Far-right political protests including white supremacy and anti-immigration activism
cases.summary: Thomas Sewell, leader of National Socialist Network, charged after violent incidents during protests in Melbourne in August 2025, including clashes at Camp Sovereignty and public marches
cases.main_issue: Whether Sewell demonstrated a compelling reason for bail and whether he posed an unacceptable risk to community safety if released
cases.outcome: Bail granted with strict conditions including residence restrictions, curfew, non-association orders, and reporting obligations
cases.sanction_type: Bail granted with conditions including curfew, residence restrictions, reporting, non-association, and bail guarantee
tags: Far-right political protests including white supremacy and anti-immigration activism

cases.case_name: Tallott v The State of Western Australia
cases.case_type: Leave to commence proceedings / Judicial review application
cases.summary: Protester alleging false imprisonment following arrest during enforcement actions directed by Premier regarding protest activities in Western Australia, 2022.
cases.main_issue: Whether leave should be granted to commence proceedings for false imprisonment and misfeasance in public office related to protest arrest and police conduct.
cases.outcome: Limited leave granted to commence proceedings for false imprisonment only; application to reopen prior discontinued matter and claim for misfeasance refused.
cases.sanction_type: Limited leave to commence proceedings granted; other claims refused

cases.case_name: The Game Meats Company of Australia Pty Ltd v Farm Transparency International Ltd
cases.court: Federal Court of Australia Full Court
cases.case_type: Appeal from judicial review and injunction application
cases.summary: Animal rights activists trespassed onto private premises to install covert video cameras capturing footage for advocacy purposes in Victoria, 2024
cases.main_issue: Whether a constructive trust should be imposed over copyright in video footage obtained through trespass and whether injunctive relief should restrain publication
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; constructive trust imposed; injunction granted restraining publication; cross-appeal on damages dismissed
cases.sanction_type: Constructive trust declaration; permanent injunction; assignment order; deletion order

cases.court: Local Court of New South Wales
acts_engaged: Hinder or resist police (statutory basis not specified)
cases.summary: Former Greens candidate Hannah Thomas arrested (and injured) at a pro-Palestine protest outside SEC Plating, Sydney.
cases.main_issue: Hindering/resisting police; failing to comply with move-on directions.
cases.outcome: All charges withdrawn by DPP, Sept 2025.

cases.case_name: Application by the Chief Commissioner of Victoria Police under s 21B of Part 3A of the Terrorism (Community Protection) Act 2003
ideology_cause: Security against terrorism threats related to political/religious visit
cases.summary: Security measures for high-profile dignitaries' visit in Melbourne amidst protest risks February 2026
cases.main_issue: Whether authorisation of special police powers under terrorism legislation is reasonably necessary to ensure safety at event
cases.outcome: Court authorised special powers for police at event areas for specified time
cases.sanction_type: authorisation of special police powers including search, cordon, seizure
tags: Security against terrorism threats related to political/religious visit

cases.case_name: Browne v Assistant Commissioner of Police, North West Metro Region
acts_engaged: Constitution (Cth) — implied freedom of political communication
Designated area declaration (Control of Weapons Act 1990 (Vic) s 10D)
cases.summary: Challenge to Victoria Police's Melbourne CBD designated-area declaration affecting protest activity.
cases.main_issue: Whether the police declaration and associated stop-and-search powers were lawful.
cases.outcome: Declaration held unlawful and invalid.

cases.summary: 2017 Invasion Day protest march in Sydney, NSW; police crowd control intervention to prevent flag burning
cases.main_issue: Whether police owed and breached a duty of care to avoid physical injury to bystanders during crowd control at protest
cases.outcome: Appeal dismissed; police owed duty of care but did not breach it; no liability to State of NSW

cases.case_name: Hoath v Queensland Police Service (Weapons Licensing Branch)
ideology_cause: Free speech, political communication related to extremist political views
cases.summary: Applicant attended protest march in Ipswich on 17 February 2024, involved with neo-Nazi and extremist groups
cases.main_issue: Whether applicant is fit and proper person to hold firearms licence given political affiliations and protest activities; whether implied freedom of political communication restricts operation of s 10B of Weapons Act 1990
cases.outcome: Hearing adjourned pending notice to Attorneys-General under s 78B Judiciary Act 1903; reasons for decision and further hearing to be scheduled
cases.sanction_type: adjournment, direction to issue s 78B notices
tags: Free speech, political communication related to extremist political views

cases.case_name: Jarrett & Ors v State of New South Wales
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales - Court of Appeal
acts_engaged: Constitution (Cth) — implied freedom of political communication
Public Assembly Restriction Declaration scheme (Terrorism (Police Powers) Act 2002 (NSW) Pt 2 Div 3A)
cases.summary: Pro-Palestine / anti-protest-law challenge by E. Jarrett, J. Lees & M. Berkon to NSW 2025-26 public-assembly restriction declaration scheme enacted after Bondi attack.
cases.main_issue: Whether recent NSW protest restrictions are constitutionally valid.
cases.outcome: The court held the three sets of provisions breached the implied freedom of political communication and the impugned provisions were declared invalid.

cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Climate change protest march organised by Blockade Australia in Sydney on 27 June 2022
cases.main_issue: Validity and legality of arrest warrant issued for protest-related charges after execution and conclusion of proceedings
cases.outcome: Extension of time refused; summons dismissed; arrest warrant not declared invalid
cases.sanction_type: dismissal of judicial review application; costs order

cases.summary: Yorta Yorta/Dja Dja Wurrung woman Ruth Langford arrested twice in 2025 for anti-logging protest; on-Country hearing requested.
cases.main_issue: Trespass and failure to comply with authorised-officer request.
cases.outcome: Pending - on-Country hearing requested.

cases.case_name: Lawton v State of Victoria (Victoria Police)
cases.case_type: judicial review of summary dismissal of discrimination and human rights claims
acts_engaged: Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act 2006 (Vic)
Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 1998 (Vic)
cases.summary: Participation in 'Freedom Rally' protest during Melbourne COVID-19 lockdown in 2021
cases.main_issue: Whether Charter of Human Rights claim can survive summary dismissal of discrimination claim under Equal Opportunity Act and whether VCAT has jurisdiction given federal issues
cases.outcome: VCAT found no federal jurisdiction issue; dismissed discrimination claim as misconceived; consequently dismissed Charter claim for lack of jurisdiction under s 75 VCAT Act

cases.case_name: Lees v State of New South Wales
cases.court: Supreme Court of New South Wales
cases.summary: Palestine Action Group organized protests against Israeli President Herzog's visit to Sydney, Feb 9, 2026
cases.main_issue: Validity of Major Events Act regulations/orders declaring Israeli Presidential Visit a major event restricting protests
cases.outcome: Plaintiff's amended summons dismissed; regulation and order valid

cases.case_name: Nona & Ors v State of Queensland & Anor
cases.summary: Indigenous students protest against racial discrimination at Cairns State High School, March 2021
cases.main_issue: Whether the school and its principal discriminated against Indigenous students and failed to provide a culturally safe learning environment, including response to a student protest
cases.outcome: Applications dismissed; no unlawful racial discrimination or victimisation by school or principal established

cases.court: Supreme Court of Victoria - Court of Appeal
cases.summary: Protest at Treasury Gardens, Melbourne during COVID-19 restrictions, 31 October 2020
cases.main_issue: Lawfulness of three arrests of protester under COVID-19 public health directions, including whether police had reasonable grounds and complied with arrest procedures
cases.outcome: Leave to appeal granted on two grounds but appeal dismissed; first and third arrests unlawful, second lawful; damages awarded $4,000; costs ordered with split liability
cases.sanction_type: damages for false imprisonment, costs order
